Building and maintaining a long-term vision and 6-month roadmap for Platform & Infrastructure.
Growing the Platform & Infrastructure team. You’ll hire ICs, managers, and build out a headcount plan. This will include determining if more specialized roles need to be established (e.g., DB Admin).

Building and maintaining an excellent relationship with Product Engineering. The ideal state is that Product Engineering can move incredibly fast independently without breaking performance or reliability, and Platform & Infrastructure doesn’t feel like they’re always cleaning up someone else’s “mess.” Today, there’s a great relationship, but there’s always room for improvement!

Assessing and improving our monitoring and incident management process. Again, we’re doing relatively well here, but there’s always room to improve. For example, making uptime measurement easier and improving coordination with Support during incidents.

Maintaining vendor relationships and negotiating pricing for our critical hosting and observability infrastructure, including AWS, ClickHouse, Datadog, and Braintrust. They have a meaningful impact on gross margin and need to be kept in check.

You’ve managed managers. Managing other leaders is a very different ball game, and not everyone enjoys it or thrives in it. Within your first 6 months, you’ll most likely have to hire a manager underneath you.

If you have experience managing developer experience and developer tools, building out a dedicated team for DevEx. If you don’t have experience here, DevEx will report into Product Engineering. Happy to discuss once we meet!

A big part of our secret sauce is how we run Engineering. We achieve incredible speed and quality by discarding many industry norms and being optimistic about Engineers. We consider what makes exceptional Engineers exceptional, then figure out how to hire them and build an environment that gives them the freedom and agency to be exceptional. You’ll be a key leader in ensuring that continues!
The Qualifications
We’re entrusting you with a company priority, so we want you to know how to scale products and build the great teams that do that. This means:

You played an important role leading a company through a high-growth period (either as an IC Lead or Engineering Leader). You had to make high-quality decisions under pressure. That often meant striking a balance between short-term fixes to keep the product from falling over and long-term investments to ensure it didn’t happen again.
You have experience hiring and building hiring processes, and enjoy it! You’ve designed interviews, interview loops, and led hiring strategy.

You have a track record of excellent collaboration with other departments. You were a key contributor to company-level initiatives that involved Product Engineering, Product, Sales, or Support. Those departments felt heard and supported, yet positively challenged by you.

You have a background in writing production software (far beyond scripts). Our Platform & Infrastructure team is exclusively made up of strong software engineers, not just folks who scale the systems software runs on. They can jump into any part of our app, understand the code, and modify the underlying logic. We expect you to have similar experience to grow and upskill the team.

You are knowledgeable about platform and infrastructure technologies, networking, and hardware. You know how Kubernetes goes beyond a Container Orchestration Platform, how traffic flows between Load Balancers and Pods, and how the intricacies of the underlying hardware can cause Cloud abstractions to break, etc.

You are a great communicator, particularly in writing. You’ll need to be able to go deep with Infrastructure Engineers in conversations while also communicating those concepts to folks like myself who have much less experience.

You should be comfortable managing a team spanning from the Americas West Coast to Europe. You’ll be able to hire managers to focus on specific time zones, but I expect you to have skips with some engineers (and you should want to, too!). To ensure a reasonable work schedule, we’re only hiring candidates who live in the PST-GMT time zone.
What We’re Building

As engineers, we are used to tooling that makes us better at what we do. When we started Ashby, we saw the opposite with Talent Acquisition software. Recruiting teams were leveling up how they did their work, but instead of software meeting this new standard, it held them back.

Scheduling a final round is an excellent example. Recruiting teams wanted to schedule candidates faster, track interviewer preparation and quality, and do it with half the headcount. A recruiter needed to manually collect availability from the candidate, identify qualified interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and make any last-minute adjustments as availability changed. They must do this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. 🥵 TA software didn’t help.

As hiring managers, we know TA is a critical function, and as engineers, we know software can do better. So, we built and continue to build Ashby to give TA teams the highest standard of tooling. Software that’s intelligent and powerful. Software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We want other functions and departments to be jealous of what TA teams can do with Ashby, and today they often are!
Why You Shouldn’t Apply
You’ve always been a line manager or never led a department within Engineering. You haven’t led the definition and evolution of culture and processes.

You don’t enjoy coding or don’t find time to stay up-to-date on technology. We believe great leaders are folks who were great engineers themselves. That starts with loving the craft and never giving it up.
You went into management because it was the only growth path available. We want folks who could have been Principal engineers (or were one!).

You're happy with a team of engineers who are predominantly early-career or mid-career or don't thrive with ownership or autonomy. You believe that with enough guardrails, the team can get things done.

To you, a Staff or Principal Engineer is someone who spends most of their time project managing or conducting architecture reviews. You don’t believe staff and principal engineers could lead by the example they set or the leverage they create through their work.

You’re not optimistic or convinced that we can build a large engineering team that functions differently from the status quo. You think, at some size, common processes need to be implemented to ensure consistent delivery (e.g., sprint planning, product managers writing in-depth specifications). You might not say it out loud, but you think, at some size, compromises have to be made for the sake of hiring numbers or consistency.
Engineering Culture

Our engineering culture is motivated by Benji’s (Co-founder and CEO) and my belief that a small, talented team, given the right environment, can build high-quality software fast (and work regular hours!). We do it through:
Minimal process with ownership over decisions normally made by product and design
Natural collaboration and deliberate communication
Investing in tools and abstractions that give us leverage, including LLM-driven dev tooling.
Putting effort into building a diverse team
Minimal Process & Lots of Ownership

The best engineers we’ve worked with delivered reliably magical outcomes. They often discovered problems, prioritized the right ones, and relentlessly drove them to solutions that were not only successful but often brilliant and creative. While they did this with minimal oversight, stakeholders were never in the dark as to what was going on, and no setback was a surprise.

Traditional development processes aren’t meant for the best engineers. Their purpose is to create consistent outcomes regardless of the engineer’s skill. But consistency comes at the expense of an engineer’s time and freedom—both ingredients necessary to generate those magical outcomes. As a result, process stifles the best engineers and doesn’t give others the opportunity to practice the behaviors that made the best engineers the “best.”

At Ashby, we want to build an environment that encourages every engineer to be their best. So, every Engineer runs their project. Product Managers (and Designers) build strategy, do customer research, and hand off problem briefs to Engineers. Engineers take on the rest: they research the problem, write product specs, build wireframes, and implement their solution end-to-end. We rely on engineers, not process, to push information outward to the relevant folks (e.g., Product Managers) and pull folks in to help (e.g., Designers, Infra). It’s a new level of ownership for many engineers, but we’d rather an engineer fail a bit and coach up their skills than use process as a crutch. Not everyone succeeds in our culture, but those who do thrive.
Collaboration is Natural & Communication is Deliberate

Our engineering team consists of lifelong learners who are talented but also humble and kind (meet them here!). These attributes create an environment where collaboration happens naturally. We combine this with research, prototyping, and written proposals to see around corners and get feedback from the team across time zones. Focus time is something that we hold sacred, and, with thoughtful and deliberate communication, engineers are in <2h meetings per week (I wrote about it here).
To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over 4 years. ~34 hours of focus time, 2.5h of interviews, and 3.5 hours of meetings:
We also meet in person at least twice a year, once as a department and once as a company. You also have a small budget to meet up with folks in your city/region.
Increase Leverage, not Team Size
We built Ashby with the quality, breadth, and depth that many customers would expect from much larger teams over larger time scales. We’ve done this through investment in:
Great developer tooling. For example, our CI/CD takes ~10m, we deploy at least 15x a day, and our debugger works out of the box. Everyone on the team has contributed to our developer experience 💪🏾.

Building blocks to create powerful and customizable products fast. At the core of Ashby is a set of common components (analytics modeling and query language, policy engine, workflow engine, design system) that we constantly improve. Each improvement to a common component cascades throughout our app (short video below).

AI-powered tooling. We think of AI as a way to automate the mundane parts of building and maintaining high-quality software. We use a combination of third-party and internally built tools that, for instance, auto-triage customer issues, suggest fixes, prototype ideas, generate production-ready code, and conduct code reviews. Engineers have an unlimited token budget (but are not measured on it). We write in detail about our philosophy, current use of AI, and future plans for AI in Engineering here.
Here’s an impromptu quote from Arjun in our company Slack of what it’s like to build a feature at Ashby:
And a demo of one of these building blocks:
Put Effort into Diversity

Diverse teams drive innovation and better outcomes. Having seen my mother and partner build their careers as minority women in non-diverse fields, I want to make sure Ashby creates opportunities for the next generation of engineers from underrepresented groups.

Today, 30% of engineers and 50% of our engineering leaders at Ashby are from underrepresented groups. We actively maintain and improve these numbers by sourcing diverse candidates, providing generous paid family leave, banning leetcode interviews, providing guidance and coaching to candidates, and more.
Work-Life Balance: It’s A Marathon, Not a Sprint

The intensity of work at Ashby should feel like a marathon, not a sprint (nor speed-walking). We work with urgency and ambition to build excellent software, but we don’t need to prove out a new software category or product-market fit. That requires ingenuity and thoughtfulness, and that doesn’t happen with unrealistic deadlines or sleepless nights.

Our remote, low-meeting, high-ownership culture gives engineers (and to a similar degree, you) a lot of flexibility in how they structure their days and weeks. In practice, that means they keep their own hours, but there will be moments of intensity, like launching their feature at our annual user conference. We offer unlimited PTO, and they actually get to use it. Some of our most exceptional engineers take almost 30 days of vacation per year.

This way of working allows many of us on the team to be active parents, including Benji and me. I block off 1.5 hours every morning to spend with my daughter and drop her off at school. Mujda (Product Engineer) puts it best in an article about us: “I can say that Ashby is a great place to be a mom… No one bats an eye if I have to take my kid to a doctor’s appointment or have to work weird hours because childcare fell through.”
Interview Process
This is an important role that will lead our Platform & Infrastructure teams now and for the foreseeable future. The interview process reflects that in both challenge and length (5 rounds, ~6.5h):
Introduction call with me (30m, live)
A technical screen where we pair in our actual codebase (1h, live)
An interview to explore your past experience as a leader (1h, live)
Interview with Colin, our Head of EMEA Engineering (45m)
Final round where you meet various folks on the team and explore leadership and technical topics (3h)

I’ll have a strong read on whether we’re trending toward an offer by Round 3. Near the end of the process, we’ll do reference checks with a former manager, two direct reports, and a peer in Engineering. Depending on my bandwidth, we may start with an additional 30m screen with a recruiter.
This is also an important decision for you, so once you start interviewing, I’m always happy to have coffee chats in person or over Zoom to get to know each other.
Your First Six Months at Ashby

Your first three months at Ashby will be spent learning about Ashby Engineering and easing into leadership. While most of your onboarding will be driven by a 6-month plan you put together (and refine over time), you’ll also ship some product changes, features, and infra changes. What better way to learn how ICs work than to be one! Don’t worry if you’re not familiar with our technologies. The team is really helpful, and our dev environment is pretty awesome: it sets up in a single script, and you’ll be able to push your first product change on day one.
You and I will do 30-day, 60-day, 90-day, and 6-month reviews to calibrate on our unique culture and how you, I, and the team will work together.
Benefits
Competitive salary and equity.
10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.
Unlimited PTO.
A minimum of 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, covered by Ashby. For folks outside the US, it may be longer to be in line with regional requirements.
Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!
$100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. In other countries, we provide high-quality supplemental health insurance for you and your dependents, also fully covered by us.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Analytics Engineering
jobs.text:
About Inroads:
Inroads applies data, analytics, technology, research, and content development to co-create services and programs that are personalized, relevant, and engaging for the communities who rely on them. Our deep understanding of digital services, policy implementation, and ways communities consume information allows us to seamlessly integrate with organizations and public sector teams to revolutionize the ways they deliver complex services at scale.
About the role:
The Associate Director, Analytics Engineering will help build and scale our Analytics Engineering function. In this leadership role, you will mentor team members, establish data quality standards across programs, and refine engineering methodologies to enhance client delivery. The ideal candidate brings a strong background in conducting code reviews, developing robust data quality testing protocols, and championing best practices to drive operational excellence for our clients.
In this position you will:
Design, implement, and maintain repeatable data quality testing methodologies and automated validation frameworks for analytics engineering team members to execute across all client programs.
Partner with Engineering and Program leadership to help stand up, scale, and mature the Analytics Engineering function by defining core processes, documentation standards, and delivery frameworks.
Provide ongoing technical guidance, coaching, and mentorship to analytics engineering team members to foster continuous growth and ensure delivery excellence.
Perform hands-on data work for critical projects and programs, stepping in to support delivery teams in executing client deliverables.
Monitor data pipelines and warehouse architectures to ensure high accuracy, reliability, and compliance across diverse datasets.
Design, refine, and champion analytics engineering best practices and workflows to optimize overall client delivery.
Conduct regular code reviews and enforce best practices for code maintainability, performance, and scalability.
Serve as the technical subject matter expert for Analytics Engineering, guiding both internal teams and external stakeholders.
Other responsibilities and duties as assigned.
What we are seeking:
8+ years in data or analytics engineering, with proven expertise in data modeling, transformation frameworks, and modern warehouse architectures (consulting or public sector experience a plus)
Experience coaching or mentoring technical team members, including conducting thorough code reviews and enforcing best practices
Proven track record of designing, implementing, and maintaining data quality testing methodologies and automated validation frameworks
Excellent communication skills, with a proven ability to translate complex technical concepts for non-technical audiences
Ability and willingness to jump into hands-on data work to support project execution and meet complex client deliverables
Strong background in establishing engineering workflows, documentation standards, and scalable practices to elevate client delivery
What We Offer:
Inroads offers a friendly work environment and competitive compensation and benefits package including:
Salary: $125,000-$140,000
Premier health insurance plan
401K matching
Unlimited vacation leave
Paid sick, personal, and volunteer leave
13 paid holidays
15 weeks paid parental leave
Professional development stipend & tuition reimbursement
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
Supportive & collaborative culture
Flexible working hours
Remote friendly (within the U.S.)
And more!
The salary range for candidates who meet the minimum posted qualifications reflects the Company’s good faith understanding and belief as to the wage range, and is accurate as of the date of this job posting.
At Inroads, we celebrate, support and thrive on differences. Not only do they benefit our services, products, and community, but most importantly, they are to the benefit of our team. Qualified people of all races, ethnicities, ages, sex, genders, sexual orientations, national origins, gender identities, marital status, religions, veterans statuses, disabilities and any other protected classes are strongly encouraged to apply. Inroads endeavors to make reasonable accommodations for qualified applicants with a disability unless the accommodation would impose an undue hardship on the operation of our business. If an applicant believes they require such assistance to complete the application or to participate in an interview, or has any questions or concerns, they should contact the Director, People Operations. Inroads participates in E-verify.
Collection of Personal Information Notice:
As you are likely aware, by submitting your job application, you are submitting personal information to our company. We collect various categories of personal information, including identifiers, protected classifications, professional or employment related information and sensitive personal information. We may retain and use this information for up to three years, in order to come to a decision on whether or not you are a good fit for our company. We may also retain or use some of this information to comply with any requirements under law, or for purposes of defending ourselves in any litigation. We do not use this information for any other purpose, or share it with third parties, unless you become an employee. To learn more, or to see our full Notice to Job Applicants, pleaseclick here.

jobs.title: Director, Product Management (Consumer)
jobs.text:
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.
About the Product team
The Product team listens to our customers’ needs and translates those insights into a clear product vision. The team works closely with design, engineering, and analytics to build scalable financial products that empower people to manage their money with confidence. We rely on empathy, curiosity, and business sense to prioritize features and improve experiences. Our role is to lead with clarity, support cross-functional execution, and champion the user in every decision.
About the role
Affirm is reinventing credit to make it more honest and friendly, giving consumers the flexibility to buy now and pay later without hidden fees or compounding interest. Our Direct to Consumer Products, Surfaces, and Growth programs are a fast-growing product set that operates with the agility of a startup while leveraging the scale of an industry leader, delivering quality Consumer Experiences to our Consumers and Growth to the business alike.
You will be a pivotal strategic leader responsible for defining the next chapter of Affirm's Consumer & Card Growth programs. You will lead a portfolio of high-impact consumer journeys that directly influence conversion, engagement, and revenue. This is a role for a seasoned product leader obsessed with consumer experiences and quality, driving Consumer Product growth ie Cards, and disrupting the payments & credit landscape
What you'll do
Strategic Leadership: Define and socialize a long-term Growth and App vision and strategy, and translate that vision into clear roadmaps and decisions that teams can execute against
Portfolio Oversight: Manage and scale a portfolio of consumer-facing surfaces, and growth platforms, including Onboarding flows, App surfaces, and platforms like Segmentation & Targeting services, ensuring a simple and consistent experience across platforms
Lead and grow a high-performing PM team. Build, mentor, and manage a team of product managers, including people managers. You'll set the bar for craft, create development paths, and cultivate a culture of ownership, rigor, and candor.
Executive Communication: Proactively align senior leadership on strategy, execution risks, and mitigation plans, ensuring organizational clarity during complex initiatives
Drive cross-functional alignment at scale: Partner with Engineering, Design, Analytics, and Revenue leaders to optimize the marketplace ecosystem, balancing merchant value with consumer experiences
Operational Excellence: Establish frameworks for rigorous experimentation and funnel analysis to drive measurable gains in completion rates and customer retention
What we look for
Experience: 10+ years of product management leadership, with a proven track record of shipping large-scale consumer products in fintech, e-commerce, or marketplace environments.
Strategic Clarity: Demonstrated ability to bring "clarity when things feel messy," turning ambiguous problems into crisp narratives and structured execution plans.
AI/LLM Fluency: Familiarity with AI-native product development, including agentic patterns and LLM-powered discovery experiences, to lead our highest-leverage bets in search
Analytical Rigor: Exceptional ability to use data (including LTV/CAC and profitability assessments) to guide prioritization and quantify the impact of product features.
People Leadership: Experience operating through layers of leadership, delegating ownership effectively, and scaling decision-making across diverse product lines.
Consumer Empathy: A "consumer-first" mindset with a high bar for design polish and a commitment to delivering honest financial products
Pay Grade - T
Equity Grade - USA 18
Employees new to Affirm typically come in at the start of the pay range. Affirm focuses on providing a simple and transparent pay structure which is based on a variety of factors, including location, experience and job-related skills.
Base pay is part of a total compensation package that may include equity rewards, monthly stipends for health, wellness and tech spending, and benefits (including 100% subsidized medical coverage, dental and vision for you and your dependents.)
USA base pay range (CA, WA, NY, NJ, CT) per year: $300,000 - $360,000
USA base pay range (all other U.S. states) per year: $267,000 - $327,000
#LI-Remote
Remote-first with flexibility built in
Affirm is proud to be a remote-first company. Most roles can be done from almost anywhere within the country of employment. Some positions may occasionally require in-person work at an Affirm office, and a few are office-based due to the nature of the work. All new hires will be invited to attend an in-person onboarding experience.
Benefits designed for you
Our benefits reflect our commitment to care, transparency, and flexibility. Here are a few highlights:
Health coverage at no cost: We cover 100% of premiums for employees and their dependents.
Spending stipends: Monthly stipends support your tech setup, and the ability to choose health and wellness options that are right for you.
Time off to recharge: Flexible time off and generous holiday calendars help you rest when you need to.
Own a piece of what you build: Our employee stock purchase plan (ESPP) lets you buy Affirm stock at a discount.
We’re committed to providing an inclusive interview process, including accommodations for candidates with disabilities. If you need support, we’re happy to help.
For positions based in San Francisco or Los Angeles: Affirm considers qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records, as required by law.
By clicking "Submit Application," you acknowledge that you have read Affirm's Global Candidate Privacy Notice and consent to the use of your personal information as described.

jobs.title: Head of Digital and Technology Solutions
jobs.text:
Main purpose of the role
CIFF aims to be more productive, data-driven and operationally agile through responsible use of technology, automation, artificial intelligence and stronger knowledge management. The vision of the Operations team is to: “PROTECT, CONNECT and EMPOWER CIFF and its partners to deliver greater impact for children by enabling the foundation to turn ambition into action, as effectively and safely as possible”. This role is responsible for implementing this vision from a digital and technology perspective, providing organisation-wide leadership for the digital and technology operating model needed to realise that ambition.
The role is accountable for CIFF’s IT service delivery, technical platforms, enterprise architecture and integrations, cyber security, reliability and technical service performance. It has overall accountability for the resilience and effectiveness of CIFF’s technology estate, technology investment, and associated enterprise technology risks.
Of particular importance is the responsible adoption of AI throughout CIFF’s operations and wider work. It enables business owners to own system purpose, outcomes, priorities, controls, processes, data definitions and outputs, while ensuring agreed changes are technically feasible, secure, integrated and sustainable.
Working through the Systems Steering Committee and in partnership with senior system owners as part of the committee, it will enable CIFF programme teams to further develop and enable data capability in strategic grantees, directly supporting sustainable delivery of CIFF’s objectives and strengthening the field. This role also oversees CIFF’s cyber security systems and culture, which is one of the top risks facing CIFF, ensuring the continuity of our operations and the security of our data is a key responsibility. A key component of the role is developing proposals and approaches for the use of technology to protect the organisation, from cyber security infrastructure to programmatic due diligence and monitoring.
The role reports to the Chief Administrative Officer and provides strategic advice to the Executive Team and Board, partners with programme and operational leaders, and develops the technical and human capability required to use technology, data and AI effectively. It also supports programme teams and selected partners on data, technology and cyber security where this advances CIFF’s missions.
The role leads the Digital & Technology Solutions (DTS) function and works closely with the staff responsible for IT Service Delivery and AI and Business Intelligence, ensuring that CIFF’s technology estate remains secure, resilient, well governed and responsive to users.
Role responsibilities
Strategy & planning
· Set and maintain CIFF’s digital and technology strategy, operating model and enterprise roadmap, aligned to CIFF’s strategic scaling approach (i.e. increasing our impact, while not increasing the operational footprint) and the organisation’s priorities for productivity, data, automation, AI and knowledge management.
· Own the technical roadmap for CIFF’s IT service delivery, shared platforms, architecture, integrations, security and reliability, and present strategic developments and material risks to the Executive Team and relevant Board committees as necessary.
· Act as the senior technical lead to the Systems SteerCo, supporting the Chair and Executive Sponsor to implement the OPS vision across systems. Provide transparent pipeline management, technical advice and prioritisation across business owners, escalating unresolved enterprise trade-offs to the Executive Sponsor or Executive Team where required.
· Provide compelling, consistent, and united leadership which creates clarity for all staff in the team across all locations and builds a sense of shared accountability for its success and that of the organisation.
· Develop and maintain excellent external relationships within the sector specialism, always acting as an ambassador for CIFF and its missions, to help build the organisation’s reputation and profile as a professional, visionary, and collaborative philanthropy, using the best technology responsibly to increase the impact of its missions for children.
· Ensure continuity of service, technology resilience and data security which supports and enables CIFFs hybrid working approach, including appropriate recovery and continuity arrangements for critical systems and services. Ensure high standards for operational performance, customer satisfaction and cyber security, and effective preparedness, escalation and response to major cyber or technology incidents. The role reports annually to the Executive Team and the Finance, Audit, and Investment Committee on cyber security, or more frequently if required as a result of incidents or specific risks.
Delivery & performance
· Work closely with and support the Head of IT Service Delivery to ensure the highest standards of IT service delivery, ensuring staff are enabled with the most effective and efficient technology products, from systems through to hardware.
· Work with the Head of AI and Business Intelligence and business owners to establish responsible AI governance, identify high-value use cases, build organisational capability, and ensure that AI tools, automation, analytics and data products are secure, ethical, well controlled and aligned to business priorities, all of which is documented and maintained in CIFF’s AI Norms of use which will be regularly reviewed and updated. Drive responsible adoption of AI and automation across CIFF, with clear measures of adoption, productivity, quality and organisational value.
· Represent CIFF with peer organisations, including COOs, CAOs and IT leads for other funders as well as our strategic grantees. Leveraging knowledge to co-create capacity building programmes for the sector, for example as part of the OPN.
· Partner with business and system owners to translate agreed outcomes, process designs, controls, data standards and service requirements into secure, integrated and deliverable technical solutions, with clear accountabilities for change approval, risk, supplier performance, continuity and decommissioning.
· Manage the enterprise pipeline and support the Systems SteerCo to prioritise system changes across business owners, with decision-making at SteerCo level and escalation to the Executive Team where required.
Leadership of the team
· Offer inspiring and motivational leadership that role models CIFF’s values and leadership behaviours and empowers and enables staff across all locations to deliver excellence.
· Adopt a coaching approach with colleagues which instils a culture of openness and trust, embraces diverse thinking, and encourages continuous improvement and learning.
· Provide ongoing support to all direct reports, ensuring high performance is enabled through objective setting, clear accountabilities, and regular review.
· Design and maintain a clear DTS operating model spanning enterprise architecture, cyber security, technical platforms and integrations, service delivery, data and business intelligence, AI enablement and system change delivery, with effective interfaces to business owners and Operations.
· Lead the DTS team and provide clear direction and accountability across the wider technology leadership structure, including the staff responsible for IT Service Delivery and AI and Business Intelligence and with the leaders of enterprise architecture and system change delivery.
Stakeholder and partner management
· Work closely with the CAO, Executive Team, Director of Operations, London, senior members of the Programme teams and forums such as the Employee Forum to keep up to date on issues, opportunities and strategies to ensure that the views of all relevant stakeholders are represented as best as possible as part of the DTS operating model and executable plans.
· Oversee strategic technology suppliers and shared technical contracts, ensuring that CIFF’s systems remain secure, resilient, highly available and cost effective. Clarify where business owners are accountable for supplier value and performance, while DTS manages technical relationships, incidents, releases, integrations and operational risk.
· Advise and support DTS team in identifying, negotiating with, and managing appropriate vendors / partners (as required), to enable CIFF to maximise its philanthropic impact through effective collaboration.

jobs.title: VP Product & Engineering
jobs.text:
Tout ce que nos clients voient et utilisent, c’est vous qui le concevez. Nous créons le poste de VP Product & Engineering pour faire de notre puissance GPU une gamme de services d’IA que les développeurs prennent en main en quelques minutes : inférence managée, déploiement de modèles, notebooks, API.
Qui sommes nous ?
Arkane Cloud est un Cloud Service Provider lyonnais, conçu pour l’IA et hébergé en Europe, avec des datacenters à Paris et à Lyon.
Notre propre infrastructure GPU permet à des startups, des chercheurs et des entreprises de déployer leurs modèles en quelques minutes, dans le respect du RGPD et jusqu’à 70 % moins cher qu’avec un hyperscaler.
Notre ambition : bâtir un acteur européen de référence de l’infrastructure IA.
Pourquoi ce poste ?
Arkane Cloud passe de 10 à 50 personnes d’ici fin 2027, et sa direction s’organise autour de deux rôles complémentaires, tous deux rattachés au CEO. Le VP Infrastructure fait tourner nos datacenters, nos serveurs GPU, le réseau et le stockage. Le VP Product & Engineering construit tout ce que nos clients voient et utilisent.
Vous dirigez deux pôles :
• Product : l’expérience de nos clients, de la console à l’onboarding, avec la documentation et l’analytics produit.
• Engineering : la plateforme elle-même : API publique, SDK et CLI, comptes et droits, facturation à l’usage, services d’IA managés.
Vos missions
• Bâtir nos services IA
• Porter la vision et la roadmap de la plateforme
• Structurer et faire grandir les pôles Product et Engineering.
• Solidifier les fondations
• Co-construire avec le VP Infrastructure les API de provisioning, les nouvelles offres GPU et leur pricing (avec le CSO), la gestion des incidents et la communication client.
Vos 6 premiers mois
• 1er mois : rencontre des clients et des équipes, état des lieux de la console, de l’API, des services d’inférence et de la facturation.
• 3 mois : roadmap produit et IA à 12 mois validée avec le CEO, organisation des pôles Product et Engineering posée, interfaces avec l’Infrastructure formalisées.
• 6 mois : un premier service IA managé lancé ou refondu, indicateurs produit suivis chaque mois, recrutements clés réalisés.
Votre expérience
• 10 ans ou plus en engineering avec une dimension produit, dont au moins 3 ans à la tête de pôles produit et techniques.
• Au moins une solution IA construite et mise en production à l’échelle : plateforme d’inférence, MLOps, API de modèles ou produit cloud pour développeurs.
Vos expertises
Indispensables :
• IA et inférence : moteurs de serving (vLLM, SGLang ou équivalent), déploiement et optimisation de modèles en production.
• Kubernetes : vous savez concevoir des services qui y tournent et dialoguer d’égal à égal avec l’équipe Infrastructure.
• Facturation à l’usage et IAM : mesure de la consommation, billing, authentification, gestion des droits.
• Management de pôles en croissance, anglais professionnel courant.
Un vrai plus :
Expérience chez un cloud provider, un neocloud GPU ou une plateforme MLOps ;
Connaissance des marketplaces de modèles.
Pourquoi nous rejoindre
• Du poids dans les décisions, vous serez rattaché au CEO, vous définissez la stratégie produit avec le VP Infrastructure.
• Une équipe à bâtir. Deux pôles, Product et Engineering, à structurer pendant le passage de 10 à 50 personnes.
• Un produit qui porte votre signature : console, API, facturation, services d’IA managés : tout ce que nos clients utilisent, c’est vous qui le concevez.
• Un cloud IA européen à construire. Un cloud GPU souverain, pour des clients qui veulent garder la maîtrise de leurs modèles et de leurs données.
Package et avantages
• 90 – 110 k€ brut annuel, BSPCE
• Deux jours de présentiel (mercredi/jeudi) pour les profils de la région lyonnaise ou deux jours toutes les deux semaines pour les profils en dehors de la région lyonnaise.
• Mutuelle à 100 %, tickets restaurant, RTT (Convention Syntec)
Arkane Cloud s’engage pour la diversité : nous étudions toutes les candidatures, sans distinction de genre, d’âge, d’origine ou de handicap.
Compensation: €90K – €110K
• €90K – €110K

jobs.title: Head of Product Engineering
jobs.text:
Location: Remote (EMEA) · Germany/Munich preferred - CET/CEST time zone
Hi — I'm Grigory, co-founder and CTO at Secfix.
At Secfix we're building security compliance systems for teams and agents to become and stay compliant with less effort. We're already the category leader in Europe. AI is changing how software gets built, and we're shaping the tools this new era requires.
I've spent most of my career believing that the best engineering leaders aren't the ones who run the most meetings. They're the ones who make everyone around them faster, clearer, and more proud of their work — and they can do that because they've been through the hard technical problems themselves.
Since we started, I've done the engineering leadership myself: 1:1s, hiring, design reviews, performance conversations. The team is 8 engineers and 2 product designers, and I'm spread across too many things. If we were a football team, we'd be a good regional side that just made it to the Bundesliga — talented, hard-working, winning quite a few games. Now we need a coach who's played at Champions League level and can take us there to win every week.
That means an engineering leader who can still ship. Someone who owns the engineering end-to-end — the technical decisions, the pace, and the people who will lead the teams —and has product taste — who notices when a feature takes three weeks that should take one, and when it ships on time but isn't good enough. You won't ship weekly — you'll need focus — but you'll build with the team often enough to know the playbook still works.
You'll work directly with me. Two things matter most here: speed and taste. Most teams pick one. We need both to win.
— Grigory
Why Secfix exists
Over 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it.
Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months.
We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to own European market from SMBs to mid market.
This space is not threatened by AI; it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of engineering work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more.
What you'll actually do in the first 3 months
This isn't a role where you show up and start running standups. There are no standups. Here's how the first quarter goes:
Month 1: Ship. Get into the codebase and ship a meaningful feature with AI alongside the team. You don't need to be the fastest engineer in the room, but the team needs to see that you can build at the level you'll ask of them and can ask the right questions.
Month 2: Make the team faster. Find where features take three weeks that should take one, and fix it — in tooling, in how we review and test, or in who's working on what. Start regular 1:1s with each engineer, focused on weekly output, quality, and how well they use AI.
Month 3: Own hiring and the team shape. Take over engineering hiring and build a process that runs without my oversight. Decide how the team is organised as it grows, and which lead roles we hire or grow into first. The next people we bring in should raise the pace again. I will be there but switch my focus to final interviews.
What will the role look like beyond the first 3 months?
After the first quarter, the job is running engineering: the organisation and the technical direction. You own how the team builds: how engineers test, how they review each other's code and security, how the team is organised, and who we hire next. We're 8 engineers and 2 product designers today and plan to be around 16 within 12 months — most of that hiring is yours to run.
You won't ship weekly, but you'll build something with the team now and then, because that's how you know the playbook still gets things out the door. Our CS and Sales leaders work the same way — they still own a small slice of the IC work, so they have skin in the game.
Here's what you'll be close to in the next months:
Speed. You’ll refine our software development processes to keep the team operating at high velocity. Cycle time from spec to production is your number and accountability. Tooling, review flow, how work is split, who's on what — whatever moves it.
Quality. Improve how engineers test and automate, how they review each other's code and security changes, and how the zero-bug policy survives a team of 20.
Organisation and leadership. Team structure, performance reviews, the hiring plan, and the managers and tech leads who will run the teams.
AI in the craft — and in the management. Engineers already work with an established set of encoded skills and rules — there's a whole playbook; you keep pushing that. Same for your own work: hiring, 1:1s, the recurring stuff.
What success looks like
At 6 months: You have shown you can be one of the top performers in the team and coached others to perform better. The hiring process runs without me, and we've added 2 engineers through it. Sales, CS, and product all feel the difference in how fast we ship — and in quality.
At 12 months: The team is around 12-16, the zero-bug policy is still holding at that size, and I'm not in the engineering critical path anymore. You've hired and grown the first engineering /tech leads, and the structure will hold through the next doubling.
How we work
We've written in depth about our engineering culture. Here's the short version — read the full articles linked below if you want the real picture.
Focus is sacred. Engineers are in fewer than 2 hours of meetings per week. We write before we meet. We use Loom for async walkthroughs, Notion for specs, Gather for pairing, and Slack only for what's urgent or lightweight. We don't do status theatre. We wrote about our thoughtful communication and our remote culture; give it a read.
To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over a year:
Small, temporary teams. A designer and two engineers. A backend engineer and a CS person. The group forms around the problem, ships, and dissolves. No standing squads, no permanent team structures — at least not yet. The people closest to the problem usually shape the solution.

jobs.title: Vice President, Solutions Engineering
jobs.text:
At OneSpan, we specialize in digital identity and anti-fraud solutions that create exceptional and secure experiences.
OneSpan is seeking a Global Vice President of Solution Engineering to lead and evolve the presales organization supporting our Cybersecurity business. Reporting directly to the Chief Revenue Officer and serving on the Revenue leadership team, this executive will be accountable for how OneSpan wins the technical decision, improves sales effectiveness, and scales solution engineering across regions.
You will build a high-performing, globally aligned organization that combines deep cybersecurity expertise with commercial judgment and a customer-outcome orientation. Your mandate includes designing the global SE operating model, developing talent, raising the quality of technical discovery and validation, and making resource investments that improve win rates, conversion, and deal velocity.
You will be a senior technical and strategic advisor to customers and an influential partner to Sales, Product, Marketing, Partnerships, and Customer Success. Success requires fluency across OneSpan’s Security portfolio—including authentication, digital identity, fraud prevention, and mobile application security—and the ability to position hardware, software, SaaS, and integrated solutions in complex enterprise environments.
What You’ll Do
Lead and Transform the Global SE Organization
Design and execute a single global SE operating model, with clear regional alignment, coverage and specialist models, rules of engagement, escalation paths, and decision rights.
Lead, coach, and retain a globally distributed team of Solution Engineers and Solution Architects; build a leadership bench, succession plans, and a culture of accountability and technical excellence.
Own capacity and investment planning, including AE-to-SE coverage, skills mix, specialist deployment, geographic allocation, and prioritization of strategic opportunities.
Build consistent performance expectations, career architecture, talent assessment, development plans, and promotion standards in partnership with People and Revenue Operations.
Partner with the CRO and regional sales leadership to align SE resources to go-to-market priorities while preserving consistent global standards.
Drive Technical Wins and Revenue Outcomes
Own the global presales strategy and execution plan supporting Security new-logo acquisition, competitive displacement, expansion, and growth across direct and partner-led routes to market.
Increase technical win rates and sales productivity by strengthening discovery, qualification, solution design, demonstrations, competitive differentiation, and customer value articulation.
Establish governance for proofs of concept, pilots, and technical evaluations, including entry/exit criteria, success measures, resource commitments, and conversion to commercial outcomes.
Be an active member of the CRO leadership team, contributing to pipeline inspection, strategic deal reviews, account planning, forecasting insight, and execution priorities.
Define and inspect an actionable SE scorecard, including technical win rate, POC-to-win conversion, technical evaluation duration, resource utilization/capacity, and deal progression; partner with Revenue Operations on data definitions.
Serve as the executive escalation point for high-stakes technical pursuits, critical competitive situations, and strategically important customer engagements.
Be a Strategic Customer and Market Leader
Engage CISOs, CIOs, fraud and identity leaders, architects, and digital channel executives as a credible advisor who connects security requirements with measurable business outcomes.
Sponsor executive briefings, architecture workshops, and complex technical evaluations for key global accounts and regulated-industry buyers.
Guide teams in navigating customer requirements spanning authentication, fraud prevention, digital identity, application security, integrations, deployment architecture, and relevant regulatory expectations.
Translate field and customer insight into clear competitive intelligence, product feedback, and strategic recommendations.
Connect the Revenue and Product Ecosystem
Build a structured voice-of-customer feedback loop with Product Management and Engineering, distinguishing critical deal blockers from broader roadmap opportunities.
Partner with Product Marketing and Sales Enablement on differentiated solution narratives, competitive plays, demos, and practical technical sales training.
Collaborate with Partnerships and Alliances on partner technical readiness, joint architectures, enablement, and complex ecosystem opportunities.
Coordinate with Customer Success and Professional Services to validate solution feasibility, manage handoffs, and identify opportunities for adoption and expansion.
Industrialize the Technical Sales Engine
Own the quality, scalability, and reliability of demos, POC platforms, reference architectures, technical collateral, and reusable field assets.
Standardize responses to RFPs, RFIs, security reviews, and technical diligence; apply automation and AI where appropriate to improve quality and turnaround time.
Build continuous portfolio and competitive enablement across SEs, sales teams, and partners, with measurable readiness and certification outcomes.
Represent OneSpan at selected customer, partner, industry, and analyst forums.
What You Bring
15+ years in enterprise cybersecurity or software presales, solution engineering, or technical consulting, including substantial experience leading regional or global SE organizations.
Demonstrated success building, scaling, or transforming a globally distributed SE function—not simply operating an established team.
Clear evidence of improving technical win rates, POC conversion, sales efficiency, or other measurable revenue outcomes through SE leadership.
Deep working knowledge of at least one core area of authentication, identity and access management, fraud prevention, digital identity, or mobile application security, with credibility across adjacent domains.
Experience selling complex enterprise solutions into financial services, government, or other regulated industries; comfort across hardware, software, SaaS, and hybrid deployments is strongly preferred.
Ability to engage credibly with C-level buyers while challenging and guiding architects, developers, security teams, and other technical stakeholders.
Practical architectural fluency in APIs, SDKs, integrations, cloud/on-premises environments, and enterprise security design; capable of leading solution decisions without needing to be the deepest individual specialist.
Strong commercial acumen and executive partnership skills, including disciplined resource allocation, deal strategy, pipeline analytics, and collaboration with global sales leaders.
Experience enabling system integrators, resellers, and technology partners; ability to lead through influence in a matrixed organization.
Excellent communication and leadership skills in English; additional languages are valued.
Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field or equivalent practical experience; advanced degree is a plus.
What Success Looks Like
In your first year, you will have established a clear global SE operating model and performance baseline; strengthened the leadership bench and technical readiness of the organization; implemented repeatable technical evaluation and deal-support standards; and demonstrated measurable improvements in technical conversion, presales efficiency, and the quality of collaboration with regional Sales and cross-functional teams.
Salary: $250,000 - $300,000 (depending on experience and qualifications) plus commission
Originally posted on Himalayas

jobs.title: Head of Product, Angling
jobs.text:
ABOUT onX
We’re a team of builders, adventurers, and risk takers using technology to help people confidently explore the outdoors. Driven by our mission to awaken the adventurer inside everyone, we build products that optimize every outdoor experience and inspire confidence to get out and go further.
We’re a high-growth tech company. The pace is fast, the work takes grit, and ambiguity is part of the job. As the world changes around us, we adapt - continuously evolving how we build, prioritize, and deliver.
Our business moves quickly, and there’s real opportunity to shape what we build next. Each of our verticals - Hunt, Offroad, Backcountry, and Fish - is at a different stage of maturity, which means the challenges you encounter and the impact you have will vary depending on where you sit and what the business needs most.
We operate with an experimentation mindset, continually iterating and improving how we solve problems. We expect our people to use the latest tooling, including AI, thoughtfully and responsibly, pairing human judgment with technology to increase quality, speed, and impact.
Our impact comes to life through the products we build, in the stories of our customers, and in our growing commitment to land stewardship and recreational access.
ABOUT THIS OPPORTUNITY
onX is seeking a Head of Product to own the next stage of growth for Angling. You will lead a high-growth consumer product on the exponential path to scale. You will set a compelling long-term vision for how we serve all 50M North American anglers and will own turning that vision into experiences that help them discover where to fish, prepare for outings, and make better decisions on the water.
Partnering with the General Manager (GM) and Chief Product Officer (CPO), you will build the team and product capabilities to turn that ambition into results. You will start with one PM reporting to you, and as the business scales you will attract and develop talent and build a world-class product organization. This is also a hands-on role: you will directly lead a meaningful product area while increasing the impact and independence of the PMs you coach.

Interest in fishing and a willingness to spend time learning directly from anglers.

jobs.title: Director of Engineering - Global, Remote
jobs.text:
TJM Labs builds AI-driven automation that strips away the repetitive, error-prone tasks slowing pharmacies down so teams can focus on patient care. Our bots handle prescription intake, fax processing, insurance workflows and more, helping pharmacies scale efficiently without adding headcount.
TJM Labs is looking for a Director of Engineering to lead and scale our engineering organization.
This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is technically credible, execution-focused, and takes ownership of results. You will develop a team of engineering managers and partner with senior leadership to turn company priorities into shipped outcomes.
What You'll Do
Lead, mentor, and grow engineering managers across multiple teams
Set clear expectations for delivery, quality, and team health
Own engineering execution, including planning, delivery predictability, and cross-team coordination
Provide technical leadership on architecture, reliability, and production issues
Define and track engineering effectiveness metrics, and improve how our teams build and ship, including through AI-assisted development
Partner with Product, Operations, and customer-facing teams to align priorities
Join customer conversations on complex integrations and technical escalations when needed
Requirements
Requirements
8+ years of software engineering experience, including significant hands-on work
4+ years of engineering management experience, including managing managers
Experience leading multiple engineering teams in a fast-growing organization
Strong background in backend and API services, third-party system integrations, and automation running in production
Experience building or leading teams that build AI-powered products and automation
Experience scaling an engineering organization through rapid growth
Track record of improving delivery, accountability, and team performance
Clear communication with technical and non-technical stakeholders, including enterprise customers
Strong sense of ownership and accountability
Benefits
Fully remote work environment.
Competitive compensation.
Meaningful projects with direct business impact.
High ownership and autonomy.
Opportunity to work with AI-driven technologies and modern development tools.
A collaborative team focused on solving real problems for healthcare customers.

jobs.title: Director of Digital & Product Management
jobs.text:
Position Summary
The Director of Digital & Product Management leads ACCC’s digital product strategy and is accountable for ensuring the organizations digital products, platforms, and experiences support its strategic, operational, and client-service objectives.
This role owns the digital product roadmap and provides leadership across the full product lifecycle from discovery and prioritization through design, development, testing, implementation, adoption, performance management, and continuous improvement. The Director serves as the primary connection between ACCC’s business areas and Information Technology, ensuring that business needs are translated into well-defined, user-centered, compliant, and measurable digital solutions.
Operating within ACCCs operating system, the Director owns the Digital & Product Management function on the accountability chart and is responsible for establishing clear priorities, rocks, scorecard measures, operating rhythms, and team accountabilities.
Primary Duties & Responsibilities
This job description does not limit management’s ability to assign or adjust duties and responsibilities at any time.
•Develop and maintain ACCC’s digital product vision, strategy, multiyear roadmap, translating organizational priorities, client needs, and operational needs into actionable initiatives.
•Establish product goals, business outcomes, success measures, and value propositions in partnership with business leaders.
•Lead a structured process for evaluating, prioritizing and managing digital product requests based on strategic alignment, user impact, risk, effort, and expected value.
•Balance new product development with enhancements, regulatory requirements, technical dependencies, platform maintenance, and defect resolution.
•Identify opportunities to improve digital client experiences, employee tools, self-service capabilities, and operational workflows.
•Partner with IT to assess feasibility, define and document requirements, manage dependencies, and support delivery.
•Oversee user acceptance testing, launch readiness, communications, training coordination, implementation, and post-launch support.
•Monitor product performance, adoption, user feedback, and business impact, using results to drive continuous improvement.
•Maintain visibility into product priorities, active initiatives, risks, dependencies, and progress, and communicate recommendations to senior leadership.
•Lead, coach, and develop the Digital & Product Management team.
•Support vendor evaluations and partnerships related to digital products and platforms.
•Ensure digital products incorporate accessibility, privacy, security, compliance, and operational considerations.
MA Pay Transparency Salary: $150,000

jobs.text:
At Vio, we believe booking accommodation should feel fair and effortless, never overwhelming or unclear.
As one of the world's fastest-growing travel tech platforms, we help millions of travelers find and book the right stay at the right price. They can book with us directly, compare offers across 100+ booking sites, or book through partners who offer our experience under their own brand.
Our goal is to help travelers book like an insider. That means cutting through the noise and complexity of hotel booking and surfacing real value with clarity, transparency, and full support. No tricks. No confusion. Just great stays, booked with confidence.
With operations in 100+ markets and growing fast, our mission is to reshape how people discover and book accommodation through technology that travelers can trust.
🔍 Who we're looking for
We're looking for a senior design leader to own Vio's whole user experience: Product Design, UX Research and Content Design, and the product outcomes they serve. You'll lead a team of around ten across design, research and content. This is a chance to build a function, not inherit one.
You'll report to our Head of Product and sit in domain leadership alongside product, engineering and commercial leaders, shaping strategy from the start. Vio runs two businesses on one platform: our consumer product, and white-label and API products for partners. Your job is to make the experience across both recognisably world-class, and to build a team that can sustain it.
☑️ What you'll do
Set the UX vision for Vio's next chapter, and bring product, engineering and commercial partners along with it.
Own user-facing outcomes with your peers, and make design's contribution measurable.
Lead Product Design, UX Research and Content Design, and design the org that brings them together in your first 90 days.
Set and hold the craft bar: run critique and product reviews, and make journeys consistent across our products and brands.
Work with Product and Engineering on how we ship, not only what we ship: bring design into problem framing early, and raise the quality of what reaches our users.
Build a team people want to join and stay in: clear ownership, air cover, real growth paths, and recognition for great work.
Stay close to the work, with ring-fenced time on north-star concepts and cross-product journeys.
Make AI part of how design, research and content work.

jobs.title: Revenue Cycle Managed Services - Senior Director of Information Technology
jobs.text:
Impact Advisors, LLC is a nationally recognized healthcare management consulting firm delivering Best in KLAS advisory, implementation, and optimization services. We are driven by a commitment to exceed client expectations and are proud to be a trusted partner to many of the nation's leading healthcare organizations. Our mission to drive patient-centered, value-driven outcomes has earned us prestigious industry accolades. To learn more about us, visit
Position Summary
The Senior Director of Information Technology leads the technology services that enable our internal operations and client-facing managed services. This role is responsible for the reliability, security, scalability, and performance of the technology environment supporting our teams and clients.
The Senior Director provides leadership across infrastructure, networking, systems engineering, application support, end-user computing, service desk operations, client connectivity, security and compliance, and technology onboarding. This individual serves as a senior escalation point for complex technology issues and works closely with operational leaders, client IT organizations, technology vendors, security teams, and other partners to ensure technology services meet business requirements and service-level commitments.
The ideal candidate is a broad, hands-on IT leader who understands the full technology stack and can translate technical requirements and issues into operational and client outcomes.
Key Responsibilities
Lead the strategy, delivery, and continuous improvement of internal and client-facing IT services.
Oversee networking, infrastructure, systems engineering, cloud services, remote connectivity, VPNs, firewalls, and related technologies.
Manage secure connectivity between company, client, vendor, and cloud environments.
Oversee application management and support, including operational ownership, maintenance, upgrades, incidents, integrations, and vendor escalation.
Manage secure file-transfer technologies, data exchanges, interfaces, and related monitoring and support.
Lead end-user computing, including hardware procurement, computer imaging, configuration, endpoint management, software deployment, patching, inventory, lifecycle management, and secure device disposition.
Oversee software licensing, deployment, renewals, technology vendors, and IT asset management.
Lead service desk operations and establish effective incident, request, problem, change, outage, and escalation management processes.
Define and monitor IT service levels, performance measures, root-cause analysis, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Own the technology workstream for new client onboarding, including network connectivity, system and application access, identity provisioning, file transfer, devices, communications, interfaces, security requirements, and support models.
Serve as a senior technology contact for client IT organizations and lead resolution of significant client-impacting technology issues.
Oversee communications technology, including collaboration, conferencing, telephony, and related services.
Partner with security, privacy, and compliance teams to maintain appropriate technology controls and support regulatory and contractual requirements.
Maintain business continuity and disaster recovery readiness for critical infrastructure, applications, connectivity, and technology services.
Manage technology vendors, contracts, licensing, budgets, capacity, and lifecycle planning.
Build, lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing IT team with clear responsibilities, operating standards, documentation, and escalation pathways.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
10+ years of progressive IT experience with significant experience across multiple areas of enterprise technology.
5+ years of IT leadership experience, preferably within managed services, healthcare, professional services, or another highly regulated environment.
Demonstrated experience across enterprise networking and infrastructure, systems and cloud engineering, identity and access management, endpoint and device management, hardware and software management, application support, service desk and IT service management, secure file transfer and system integrations, telecommunications, cybersecurity, compliance, and business continuity.
Experience managing geographically distributed technology environments and users.
Experience supporting client-facing technology services and working directly with client IT organizations.
Experience establishing and managing SLA-based services, major incidents, escalations, and root-cause resolution.
Demonstrated experience managing technology vendors, contracts, licensing, budgets, and technology investments.
Strong leadership, communication, problem-solving, and client relationship skills.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience supporting healthcare operations, managed services, or revenue cycle environments.
Familiarity with EHR and healthcare applications such as Epic or Oracle Health.
Knowledge of healthcare integrations and data exchange, including APIs, HL7/FHIR, X12 EDI, ETL, SFTP, and clearinghouse connectivity.
Experience with Microsoft 365, Microsoft Azure, identity management, and enterprise endpoint-management technologies.
ITIL, CISSP, CISM, PMP, Microsoft, Cisco, or comparable technical or leadership certifications.
For salaried positions, this role may also be eligible for an annual performance bonus. Additional benefits and perks may also be available, depending on the position and employment terms. This range reflects consideration of several factors, including skills, experience, training, certifications, and organizational needs.
Our People and Culture
At Impact Advisors, we cultivate a caring, fun, honest, and autonomous work environment. Our success stems from our associates' dedication and a shared mission to create a “Positive Impact.” We embrace diversity and inclusion, fostering an environment where all employees feel valued and empowered.
Join Impact Advisors and make a real difference in healthcare.
