jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.text:
Parallax Innovations is a civic communications lab building modern persuasion infrastructure for the movement to improve American democracy and elections.
We support organizations and campaigns advancing nonpartisan democracy reforms through our narrative intelligence platform. We combine technology, data, and services to help our partners reach, engage, and persuade voters in our fast-evolving information ecosystem. We enable partners with strategic guidance and hands-on production and editing support to build strong vertical-video operations across TikTok, Reels, and Shorts. Our products make it easier for campaigns to mobilize supporters as creators, equipping them with tools that draw on our intelligence and predictive capabilities to improve content before it ships. And our data assets – including an enriched voter file with audience-specific insights – help campaigns deploy and amplify the right content to the specific voters they need to reach.
Our primary focus is solving the Primary Problem—a system of party primaries that excludes millions of voters and rewards elected leaders for answering to a narrow partisan electorate. We help advance open primaries that give voters more voice and choice and leaders stronger incentives to represent their communities.
Parallax is incubated by Unite America, and is based in Denver.
As Chief Technology Officer, you will own the ongoing development and improvement of Parallax's primary competitive advantage: a narrative intelligence platform that learns what persuades Americans on reform issues, and how. You own everything engineering, AI, data, privacy & compliance, infrastructure, security, with strong influence over adjacent workflows. You also serve as an organizational leader, driving strategy and organization prioritization.
We approach persuasion like infrastructure: a lasting capability that helps the movement learn, improve and win across campaigns and election cycles. Our ambition is to build a closed-loop learning system that gets smarter every time we speak. Its AI core will connect the content we create with engagement data, audience research and experiments to learn which messages, messengers and formats work with which voters—and feed those lessons back into how we create, target and distribute the next communication.
Over each election cycle, Parallax will support a number of reform campaigns, many of them ballot initiatives. Each campaign has to reach different audiences: progressives, conservatives, independents, and the large group of Americans who are disengaged or simply worn out by politics. Our product lowers the barrier for supporters to become compelling content creators, and our platform provides guidance on frames, formats, messengers and messages are likely to work.
This is an executive role requiring technical depth and a hands-on approach to using modern engineering tools, as well as broader organizational leadership skills. You’ll craft the product vision, lead the contract engineers in developing the platform, and be the decision-maker about architecture, models, data and resources. You’ll also champion the technical vision, progress, and investment requirements to executive leadership, the Board, and potential investors. You will inherit a contract data and engineering team, and from there you will determine how the team develops, including budget development and hiring.
You will serve as a senior executive responsible for the technical integration of Parallax’s data, products, and services. Alongside the Chief of Staff and VP of Product & Partnerships, you will develop and drive organizational strategy, translate priorities into work plans and budgets, and align the team around measurable results. Ideal candidates for this role will have the judgment and management ability to assume broader organizational leadership as Parallax grows.
This role reports to the President, and is based in Denver. Relocations welcome. Exceptional candidates based elsewhere will be considered if they can commit to periodic trips to Denver.
These will be your accountabilities:
Own the development of Parallax’s core technology and competitive advantage.
Set platform strategy and capabilities roadmap: what it should measure, what its learning agenda will be, what inputs it expands to include, and how it learns and improves quarter over quarter.
Define the scoring framework: how content engagement and persuasion are quantified for Parallax, how they are weighted, and how scores connect to real outcomes.
Extend our intelligence platform beyond transcript-analysis so that it evaluates videos, including visuals, presenters, format and production choices.
Make the model decisions: which commercial and open models to use and route between, whether fine-tuning or custom components are worth it, and the tradeoffs in cost, speed and accuracy.
Build the data loop so that performance data from platforms, partners, audience surveys and experiments flows back into the platform cleanly and in an accretive fashion.
Oversee the development of dashboards and reporting that can explain what the platform is accomplishing, for internal and partner audiences.
Ensure the platform adheres to data compliance laws and a set of AI ethics guidelines which will need to be fully articulated (e.g. no deceptive or synthetic content).
Prove that it works, explain its limits.
Design and run the platform validation agenda: back-test against historical content, compare predictions with actual results, and check findings against survey and experimental (including RCT) evidence.
Build the evals and guardrails that let the platform learn within defined limits, so its outputs can be trusted and explained.
Report clearly to leadership, funders and partners on what the intelligence platform can tell us today, how confident we are, and what it cannot yet do.
Turn intelligence into decisions.
Translate platform findings into clear, weekly guidance the creative team uses on frame, format, messenger and audience.
Work with the Creative studio and Partners team to support mapping the message-by-audience grid across active campaigns: what has been tested, what is working, and where the gaps are.
Help package Parallax's intelligence effectively so that partner organizations and campaign teams can use it to make more persuasive content themselves.
Shape our technology ecosystem, build the team as needed.
As the platform expands, expand your influence and help shape the roadmap for Parallax's other internal tools and products so they effectively interoperate with the core, working closely with the people who build and deploy them.
Take over the current contractor-based data and engineering squad; decide what to keep, build or buy. Own team development, budget, and hiring, in collaboration with leadership.
Build alongside the team with the latest AI tools, and set the standard for how Parallax uses AI responsibly.
Help the President and leadership team set Parallax's strategy, and work closely with the Chief of Staff and the VP of Product & Partnerships on org-wide initiatives.
What success looks like:
First 60 days: you’ve facilitated a shared platform vision that is in sharp focus, pulled together a leadership-approved roadmap and clear technical ownership. An initial intelligence platform scoring framework should be in place to enable the creative team to run strong week-to-week experiments, learn from results, and make each round of communications smarter.
First six months: a working feedback loop connecting content, audience and outcome data; initial scoring and predictive capabilities tested against results; and initial integrations with the partner voter file and Partner Portal. The team should be using findings to improve communications, with clear measures of progress and priorities for what comes next.

jobs.title: Director of Product Engineering
jobs.text:
Hometrack is seeking an accomplished Director of Product Engineering, to lead our efforts in building innovative mission critical products to power property decision making in the UK financial services industry. We offer a competitive salary, fantastic benefits, and flexible, hybrid working.
Hometrack’s market-leading property data sets, valuation models, and risk insights are delivered via our suite of B2B SaaS applications for mortgage lenders, brokers, and more. We’ve led the market for over twenty years!
Our services are mission-critical to the UK’s top banks, automating their mortgage offers. They’re used daily by home builders, mortgage brokers, local councils, and more to make informed property purchasing decisions. We have an exciting strategy to serve an even wider section of the market, with innovative products and services.
The Director of Product Engineering will provide senior technology leadership for Hometrack’s key product lines, owning the technical strategy, delivery oversight, and evolution, providing a highly utilised and relied upon set of capabilities for clients.
This role will lead an established set of teams as they evolve and support our existing capabilities to scale and meet developing client needs. The Director of Product Engineering will collaborate closely with Product peers and wider business stakeholders to shape the long‑term roadmap, ensure robust technical foundations, and guide our continued growth.
Key Responsibilities
Strategic Leadership
Own the technology strategy ensuring alignment with our wider platform and technology strategy.
Partner with key stakeholders in product, commercial and delivery to define and evolve a clear, credible roadmap covering near‑term delivery and longer‑term technical direction.
Provide domain leadership and technical challenge
Delivery & Execution
Provide senior oversight of existing product engineering teams, ensuring delivery remains on track as the products evolve and new products are introduced.
Ensure strong engineering fundamentals, including resilience, scalability, security, and operational readiness, appropriate for an institution supporting banks and other major lenders.
Support the evolution of a highly utilised set of capabilities as they scale to meet future client needs.
Technology & Architecture
Guide architectural decisions in partnership with technical peers (Principal/Staff Engineers).
Act as a key contributor in setting our technology direction
People & Leadership
Lead and develop engineers and engineering managers (software and data).
Set clear expectations, provide coaching, and build a culture of ownership, learning, and delivery.
What We’re Looking For
Essential Experience
Senior technology leadership experience (Head of/Director or equivalent) preferably within or adjacent to financial services.
Demonstrable experience owning and evolving complex platforms, preferably in a high availability environment.
Proven ability to partner effectively with Product leadership to shape and deliver long‑term strategy.
Strong fundamental background in software engineering (.Net/AWS/Azure)
Beneficial Experience
Experience of evolving team working practices towards increasingly agentic SDLCs
Experience managing and leading data engineering teams
Leadership & Behaviours
Pragmatic and outcome‑focused, with sound judgement to balance speed, risk, and long‑term value.
Comfortable operating in ambiguity and guiding teams through an evolving domain.
Clear communicator who can explain complex concepts to both technical and non‑technical audiences.
Role‑model for Hometrack’s Behaviours and expectations around ownership, delivery, and collaboration.

jobs.title: Head of Data & Data Products
jobs.text:
WME is looking for a Head of Data & Data Products to build the next generation of our data capability.
WME sits at the center of entertainment, representing leading artists, creators, athletes, brands, and intellectual property around the world. Every day, our teams generate and work with an extraordinary amount of information about relationships, opportunities, deals, audiences, markets, and outcomes.
We believe that data can become a meaningful competitive advantage for WME — not simply by producing more reports, but by making our collective knowledge easier to access, understand, and act on.
This role will lead that evolution.
You will own WME's data product strategy, self-service analytics, shared business definitions, domain intelligence, and the business roadmap for predictive and decision-support capabilities. You will also help us rethink how the third-party data we license can become a reusable capability across our products and businesses.
The goal is straightforward: turn WME's data into products and intelligence that help our people make better decisions, identify opportunities, serve clients, and grow the business.
What You'll Do:
Build WME's Data Product Strategy
Define and lead a data product roadmap tied to real business decisions and opportunities.
Turn important datasets into trusted, reusable products rather than inputs to individual reports.
Identify where recurring analytical needs should become self-service capabilities and where expert analysis remains the better answer.
Define the users, business meaning, quality expectations, access requirements, and success measures for major data products.
Measure adoption and business impact, and continuously improve what we build.
Make Trusted Data Easier to Use
Modernize WME's self-service analytics and reporting capabilities.
Make common business questions easier to answer without requiring an analyst for every request.
Give users the context they need to understand what a metric means, where it came from, how current it is, and when it should be used.
Establish shared definitions for critical business concepts and improve consistency across teams and systems.
Reduce duplicated and bespoke reporting through reusable datasets, metrics, and analytical products.
Turn Data Into Intelligence
Identify where WME's proprietary data can reveal opportunities, patterns, and insights that aren't visible through external market data alone.
Build domain intelligence capabilities that combine deep understanding of our businesses with strong analytical judgment.
Own the business roadmap for capabilities such as matching, predictive pricing, demand forecasting, relationship intelligence, recommendations, opportunity detection, and anomaly detection.
Determine when sophisticated modeling is warranted — and when a simpler analytical approach will produce a better result.
Define success in business terms such as revenue, conversion, pricing, productivity, targeting, and client outcomes.
Make More of Our External Data
WME licenses valuable data across entertainment, audiences, media, touring, brands, and other markets.
You will:
Develop the product strategy for making those sources more reusable across WME.
Partner with research, engineering, procurement, and business teams to identify the sources that create the most value.
Help move external data from isolated reports into reusable datasets and capabilities.
Measure utilization and value to inform which sources we retain, expand, replace, or retire.
Explore opportunities to combine proprietary and external data in ways that create differentiated capabilities for WME and our clients.
Build the Function
Build and lead a focused team with strong analytical, business, and product judgment.
Develop domain expertise around the areas where WME has the greatest opportunity to create value from data.
Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Finance, Research, Operations, Cybersecurity, and business leaders across WME.
Establish clear standards for data quality, definitions, governance, measurement, and responsible use.
Create leverage through strong systems, shared capabilities, automation, and partnerships rather than simply adding headcount.
How You'll Work
This is not a traditional reporting leadership role.
You will spend significant time understanding how WME's businesses work, how decisions get made, and where better information could change an outcome.
You'll move between strategy and execution: defining a multi-year direction while helping teams solve practical problems today.
You'll work closely with our Product and Engineering organization. Engineering owns the technical data platform, including data engineering, pipelines, APIs, infrastructure, and production ML. You will own the business and product side of the data strategy: what we should build, why it matters, how it should be understood, and whether it is creating value.
You'll also partner with specialist teams across WME, including Finance and WME Insights, rather than trying to centralize every form of analysis into one organization.
What We're Looking For
Significant experience leading a data, analytics, data product, or applied intelligence function.
A track record of turning data into products or capabilities that people actually use.
Strong product judgment and the ability to distinguish an interesting analytical problem from a valuable business problem.
Experience building self-service analytics or data products without sacrificing context, quality, or governance.
Strong analytical fluency and comfort challenging assumptions, evaluating evidence, and communicating uncertainty.
Experience partnering closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science/ML, and senior business leaders.
Technical fluency across modern data platforms, warehouses/lakes, APIs, BI, data quality, metadata, access controls, and predictive modeling concepts.
Experience working with third-party data providers and finding ways to reuse licensed data across products and workflows.
Strong executive communication skills and the ability to translate complex analytical or technical ideas into clear business decisions.
Comfort operating in a complex organization where valuable knowledge is distributed across people, systems, and teams.

Data is a product. A dataset creates value when people can find it, understand it, trust it, and use it repeatedly.
Start with the decision. The goal isn't more sophisticated analysis. It's better decisions and better outcomes.

Build for leverage. You look for reusable capabilities, automation, and strong partnerships before solving a problem with additional headcount.

Most importantly, WME gets better at using what it collectively knows to identify opportunities and advocate for our clients.

jobs.title: Director, Data Strategy & Analytics
jobs.text:
Director of Data Strategy & Analytics
Job Location: US, Remote. Candidate must reside and work within the US.
Job Overview:
Lexia's data assets are central to how we grow and how we demonstrate impact. We are seeking a Director of Data Strategy & Analytics to lead the team that turns those assets into insight and action across the business, in alignment with our vision.
Reporting to the VP, Strategic Planning & Business Enablement, the Director will lead Lexia's internal business analytics function, directly managing a team of analysts and combining human analyst work with AI-enabled, self-service capabilities to maximize the use and business impact of our engineered data assets. The Director will be the primary analytics partner to Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and the Lexia executive team, and will own strategy and governance for our BI and analytics systems.
Reporting to this role is the leader of the Data Engineering team, responsible for data infrastructure and architecture. The Director of Data Strategy & Analytics will provide strategic leadership across both analytics and data engineering to ensure our data ecosystem enables business insights while maintaining the integrity, security, and confidentiality of enterprise data assets.
Job Responsibilities:
Team Leadership & Development
Develop and execute a comprehensive strategy for data and analytics that aligns with the organization's mission, vision, and strategy, leveraging data to optimize decision-making, increase operational efficiency, and maximize impact.
Manage, mentor, and develop a team of analysts, providing regular feedback and fostering a collaborative and high-performing environment.
Own project management and prioritization for all business analytics work, including analyst and AI-enabled analytics projects, and oversee review and QA to ensure data products meet high standards for quality/accuracy, user-centricity, and action-oriented data storytelling.
Support the Director of Analytics Engineering and foster a culture of continuous learning and development across the Data Strategy & Analytics team, promoting collaboration, innovation, and excellence.
Business Analytics & Insights
Drive analyst efforts to mine revenue, operational, and customer data and turn them into insightful KPIs, models, and dashboards that help our teams pursue revenue optimization and operational efficiency.
Partner with stakeholder teams across the organization to identify opportunities for leveraging data to drive innovation and improve operational efficiency.
Self-Service & AI-Enabled Analytics
Develop and maintain a scalable suite of self-service dashboards, AI agents, and conversational interfaces that enable non-technical staff to ask and answer questions of our data directly.
Establish enablement frameworks for self-service analytics that drive adoption, empower users, and provide guardrails to ensure effective and appropriate use.
In partnership with Analytics Engineering, oversee the integration of AI capabilities into analytics tools and workflows to scale self-service and operational efficiency.
Cross-Functional Partnership
Serve as the main point of contact and key data partner for Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and senior leadership, ensuring the alignment of analytics efforts with business needs and priorities.
Serve as the main point of contact for Cambium and Veritas analytics requests and collaborations, delegating to and partnering with the Director of Analytics Engineering as appropriate.
Translate business needs into clear downstream data requirements and metric definitions, partnering with the Director of Analytics Engineering to ensure the right data warehouse marts and Tableau Cloud data sources are provisioned, and providing input into data architecture, integration, and AI infrastructure decisions.
Analytics Systems, Tools & Governance
Own Tableau/BI system strategy and governance, in collaboration with other analyst teams across the organization.
Lead vendor and tool procurement and management for analytics systems and team tools, in consultation with the Director of Analytics Engineering.
Chair Lexia's cross-functional data governance group, collaborating closely with Legal, IT, and data leads to establish and maintain data and AI governance policies, procedures, and controls, and own policy compliance and appropriate sensitive data usage across DS&A-owned systems, staff, and products.
Stay abreast of emerging trends and technologies in advanced analytics, AI, and data management, and provide strategic recommendations for business innovation and responsible use.
Job Requirements:
Bachelor's degree in data science, statistics, economics, business, computer science, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
10+ years of experience in analytics, data strategy, or a related field, with a proven track record of delivering data-driven solutions that drive business impact.
5+ years of experience managing, coaching, or leading data analysts or analytics teams.
Exceptional leadership and management skills, with experience leading high-performing teams in a fast-paced and dynamic environment.
Excellent quantitative and analytical skills with experience in data visualization, statistical modeling/machine learning, and go-to-market domain analyses (e.g., campaign attribution, price sensitivity, account scoring, retention/churn analysis).
Professional proficiency in analytics and BI tools that align with our tech stack (e.g., SQL, Tableau, Python or R), and working knowledge of data engineering and cloud data platforms (e.g., Dbt, Redshift, AWS) sufficient to partner effectively with Analytics Engineering.
Experience owning BI platform strategy and governance, and managing analytics vendor and tool relationships.
Expertise in data management, including metric definition, data governance, and data quality management.
Demonstrated experience building or implementing AI-assisted analytics workflows, such as AI agents, natural language query interfaces, or LLM-driven analytics, with a deep understanding of the data privacy, security protocols, and ethical governance required to deploy them, including hallucination guardrails.
Familiarity with sales and customer data platforms (e.g., Salesforce) and experience within a SaaS B2B or B2G organization preferred.
Excellent communication, data storytelling, and collaboration skills, with the ability to translate complex data insights into clear, actionable recommendations for executive and non-technical audiences.
Strategic mindset and the ability to manage challenging priorities across multiple stakeholders.
To learn more about our organization and the exciting work we do, visit .
Remote First Work Environment
Our Remote First approach gives employees the flexibility and trust they need to effectively balance work with life. It creates a culture in which all employees are valued and where success is measured in results. It allows us to work collaboratively, inclusively and for greater positive impact, regardless of our individual locations.
If you will be working remotely, either occasionally or on a permanent basis, you must have a reliable internet connection through a cable or fiber-optic broadband service with minimum speeds of 10 Mbps download and 5 Mbps upload.
The successful candidate will be expected to actively participate in video-based interviews during the recruiting process and ongoing virtual meetings with their camera on, as part of their role. To maintain confidentiality and ensure a fair evaluation process, the use of note-taking tools, reference materials, or AI-powered tools (including generative AI, language models, or similar technologies) during interviews or other selection activities is prohibited unless prior written approval has been obtained from the People Experience team. If you require an exception for medical, accessibility, or other reasons, please contact your Talent Acquisition team member to discuss accommodations in advance.
As part of our Remote-First benefits, Cambium offers reimbursement to help cover the cost of setting up your home or remote office.
An Equal Opportunity Employer
We are dedicated to fostering a culture that celebrates unique backgrounds, ideas, and experiences. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without discrimination on the basis of race, color, age, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender, gender identity/expression, or sexual orientation), national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or genetic information (including family medical history).
We will provide reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities. You may request an accommodation during the recruiting process with your Talent Acquisition team member.

jobs.title: Executive Director, Technology
jobs.text:
About Endpoints News Media Company, LLC
Endpoints News, founded in 2016, is a leading news media company with a clear mission: to deliver the best news product in biopharma and be the essential daily read for industry leaders globally. Now a part of the Financial Times family, Endpoints News has 290,000+ registered readers and continues to grow its reach with breaking news, in-depth analysis, live and virtual events and award-winning journalism.
The Role
This is a leadership role. You lead the technology function across engineering, delivery and operations: setting the standard, making the calls, growing the people, running the work, and answering to the business for what it delivers.
You also ship. The team is small and everyone at Endpoints is an IC at some level, including the people who lead. You'll be in the codebase every week and carrying real work of your own, because that's how things get built here and because it's the only way to lead a team this size credibly.
You'll report to the SVP, Design, Product and Technology and work alongside them daily. A lot of the job is the two of you thinking out loud: what's worth building, what it would take, what it would cost. You'll help shape the technical strategy together (architecture direction, build-versus-buy, where the platform goes next), with the SVP owning the final call and the direction for product and design. The technical thinking is yours, and we'd much rather hear "here's how we could do that" than "here's why we can't".
You'll be the technology counterpart to editorial and commercial leadership. The remit is wider than engineering. Delivery, technical program management, the operational layer, the business systems the company runs on, and the vendors who extend the team all sit with you, and the team beneath you will grow to reflect that.
This role is based in the United States and is fully remote.
What You'll Do
Lead and grow the technology team across engineering, delivery and operations. Own the people side fully — hiring, performance, development and the hard conversations — and manage through a manager as the function scales.
Shape the technical strategy with the SVP — architecture direction, build, buy and integrate calls, and where the platform needs to go next. The SVP owns the final decision; you own the thinking that informs it and the delivery that follows.
Turn product direction into shipped work. Own everything between the outcome, standard and date and working software in production — scoping, technical requirements, sequencing, and the commitments we make back to editorial and business stakeholders.
Run delivery across the technology function. Own the cadence, the dependencies and the visibility that lets the rest of the company know what's coming and when.
Answer for what the team ships. Set the standard, review architecture and overrule it on technical grounds where required, and put mechanisms in place that catch problems before production.
Ship code every week. The team is small and everyone here builds, including the people who lead. You'll carry real work of your own — the hard problems, the spikes that set direction, the things that have to land — alongside the team rather than above it.
Stand up new products and evolve the existing ones across news, subscriptions and identity, data and events, including the wind-down of what the new platform replaces.
Lead security across everything we run: what's exposed, who has access, what's still running that shouldn't be, third-party risk, and the response when something happens.
Own the content and data spine. You and your team build the spine, not the surface: the interface is design's - our designers author the design system and ship it to production themselves. Shape the content model, keep the CMS moving, build the APIs and MCP services every surface and every team draws on, and finish that shift across the rest of the estate.
Own the operational layer — environments, CI, previews, observability, and the road to production that lets a designer ship with confidence.
Own the internal systems and tooling the business runs on — the integrations across CRM, events, email and subscriptions, and the services that let business teams work directly with our own data.
Direct the contractors and vendors who extend the team, and hold their output to the same standard as our own.
Get sound AI-assisted work from non-engineers live quickly, and know when it isn't sound.
Partner with editorial and business leadership to turn ideas into shipped features at the pace a newsroom requires.
Technical Requirements
Our actual stack, not a generic list. We care more about depth than about covering every line.
Hands-on, Every week
TypeScript, Node.js, modern tooling
Payload CMS on PostgreSQL, or equivalent depth in a headless, code-first CMS
Content modeling and API design — GraphQL and REST
Next.js, and Astro with React islands
Application security — authentication and authorization you can demonstrate are enforced, secrets management, dependency hygiene, least privilege
LLM-native workflow — AI tools as a core part of how you and your team build, and knowing where not to use them
Depth you've built before, even where you now direct it
Identity and payments — SSO/OIDC (we run Logto), Stripe, entitlements, paywall logic
AWS — Lambda via OpenNext, S3, CloudFront, IAM, RDS — and containers on Kubernetes
Security operations — attack surface and asset inventory, decommissioning, access lifecycle, credential rotation, logging that can answer a forensic question
Incident response — containment, evidence, and reporting that states what the logs show
Privacy and compliance — GDPR and CCPA, consent and tracking, data retention
PHP, MySQL, Python/FastAPI, Elasticsearch, message brokers
What We're Looking For
A leader first. 5+ years leading technical teams, including managing engineers directly and managing through other managers. You've hired, developed and exited people, set a team's standard, and been accountable for what it delivered.
And a builder every week. Everyone at Endpoints contributes as an IC at some level, and at this team size that includes you. You'll be writing and shipping production code regularly, not symbolically.
Leadership beyond engineering. You've owned delivery, operations, vendor relationships and stakeholder commitments — not just the codebase — and you've been the person the business holds to account for technology outcomes.
And a builder every week. Everyone at Endpoints contributes as an IC at some level, and at this team size that includes you. You'll be writing and shipping production code regularly, not symbolically.
You take a short ask and build the right thing. A sentence of business intent is enough for you to come back with what it means technically, what it costs and what it breaks.
Real backend and infrastructure depth, even where you no longer use it daily. You'll be accountable for work you don't write.

blocks.text: About Endpoints News Media Company, LLC

Endpoints News, founded in 2016, is a leading news media company with a clear mission: to deliver the best news product in biopharma and be the essential daily read for industry leaders globally. Now a part of the Financial Times family, Endpoints News has 290,000+ registered readers and continues to grow its reach with breaking news, in-depth analysis, live and virtual events and award-winning journalism.
The Role

This is a leadership role. You lead the technology function across engineering, delivery and operations: setting the standard, making the calls, growing the people, running the work, and answering to the business for what it delivers.

You also ship. The team is small and everyone at Endpoints is an IC at some level, including the people who lead. You'll be in the codebase every week and carrying real work of your own, because that's how things get built here and because it's the only way to lead a team this size credibly.

You'll report to the SVP, Design, Product and Technology and work alongside them daily. A lot of the job is the two of you thinking out loud: what's worth building, what it would take, what it would cost. You'll help shape the technical strategy together (architecture direction, build-versus-buy, where the platform goes next), with the SVP owning the final call and the direction for product and design. The technical thinking is yours, and we'd much rather hear "here's how we could do that" than "here's why we can't".

You'll be the technology counterpart to editorial and commercial leadership. The remit is wider than engineering. Delivery, technical program management, the operational layer, the business systems the company runs on, and the vendors who extend the team all sit with you, and the team beneath you will grow to reflect that.
This role is based in the United States and is fully remote.
What You'll Do

items: Lead and grow the technology team across engineering, delivery and operations. Own the people side fully — hiring, performance, development and the hard conversations — and manage through a manager as the function scales.

Shape the technical strategy with the SVP — architecture direction, build, buy and integrate calls, and where the platform needs to go next. The SVP owns the final decision; you own the thinking that informs it and the delivery that follows.

Turn product direction into shipped work. Own everything between the outcome, standard and date and working software in production — scoping, technical requirements, sequencing, and the commitments we make back to editorial and business stakeholders.
Run delivery across the technology function. Own the cadence, the dependencies and the visibility that lets the rest of the company know what's coming and when.
Answer for what the team ships. Set the standard, review architecture and overrule it on technical grounds where required, and put mechanisms in place that catch problems before production.

Ship code every week. The team is small and everyone here builds, including the people who lead. You'll carry real work of your own — the hard problems, the spikes that set direction, the things that have to land — alongside the team rather than above it.
Stand up new products and evolve the existing ones across news, subscriptions and identity, data and events, including the wind-down of what the new platform replaces.
Lead security across everything we run: what's exposed, who has access, what's still running that shouldn't be, third-party risk, and the response when something happens.

Own the content and data spine. You and your team build the spine, not the surface: the interface is design's - our designers author the design system and ship it to production themselves. Shape the content model, keep the CMS moving, build the APIs and MCP services every surface and every team draws on, and finish that shift across the rest of the estate.
Own the operational layer — environments, CI, previews, observability, and the road to production that lets a designer ship with confidence.
Own the internal systems and tooling the business runs on — the integrations across CRM, events, email and subscriptions, and the services that let business teams work directly with our own data.
Direct the contractors and vendors who extend the team, and hold their output to the same standard as our own.
Get sound AI-assisted work from non-engineers live quickly, and know when it isn't sound.
Partner with editorial and business leadership to turn ideas into shipped features at the pace a newsroom requires.

blocks.text: Technical Requirements
Our actual stack, not a generic list. We care more about depth than about covering every line.
Hands-on, Every week

items: TypeScript, Node.js, modern tooling
Payload CMS on PostgreSQL, or equivalent depth in a headless, code-first CMS
Content modeling and API design — GraphQL and REST
Next.js, and Astro with React islands
Application security — authentication and authorization you can demonstrate are enforced, secrets management, dependency hygiene, least privilege
LLM-native workflow — AI tools as a core part of how you and your team build, and knowing where not to use them

blocks.text: Depth you've built before, even where you now direct it

items: Identity and payments — SSO/OIDC (we run Logto), Stripe, entitlements, paywall logic
AWS — Lambda via OpenNext, S3, CloudFront, IAM, RDS — and containers on Kubernetes
Security operations — attack surface and asset inventory, decommissioning, access lifecycle, credential rotation, logging that can answer a forensic question
Incident response — containment, evidence, and reporting that states what the logs show
Privacy and compliance — GDPR and CCPA, consent and tracking, data retention
PHP, MySQL, Python/FastAPI, Elasticsearch, message brokers

jobs.title: Head of Engineering, NIRA
jobs.text:
Join the Tilt team
At Tilt, we see a side of people that traditional lenders miss. Our mobile-first products and machine learning-powered credit models look beyond credit scores, using over 250 real-time financial signals to recognize real potential. With millions of customers worldwide, we're not just changing how people access financial products — we're creating a new credit system that backs the working, whatever they're working toward.
The Opportunity: Senior Engineering Manager, Nira
We’re looking for a Senior Engineering Manager to lead our NIRA team, owning engineering across product, platform reliability, data infrastructure, and internal tooling. This is a high-impact role where you’ll work closely with Product, Data Science, Credit, and Marketing to build, scale, and improve a fast-growing business.
Location: Bengaluru, India (Hybrid)
How you'll make an impact
Own and execute the engineering roadmap across NIRA
Raise the bar on engineering practices (CI/CD, testing, reliability, observability)
Lead and grow a high-performing team of engineers
Drive technical decisions that balance speed, quality, and scalability
Partner cross-functionally to deliver meaningful business outcomes
Why you're a great fit
7+ years in engineering, with 3+ years in management
Experience leading teams in startup or scaling environments
Strong track record improving engineering standards and delivery
Comfortable operating across product, infrastructure, and data
Clear communicator with a bias for action
Our Interview Process
Initial Recruiter Call: A conversation to learn about your experience and what you're looking for in your next role.
Hiring Manager Interview: A deeper discussion about your experience.
Skills Panel: Meet with Tilt team members to discuss your expertise and problem-solving approach.
Leadership Conversation: A final conversation with a leader to discuss how you'll contribute to Tilt's mission, and how we can help you achieve your career goals along the way.
Don’t meet every qualification? We care about potential over your past. If you're bringing ambition and drive to what we're building, we want to hear from you.
What you'll get at Tilt
Virtual-first teamwork: The Tilt team is collaborating across 14 countries, 12 time zones, and counting. You’ll get started with a WFH office reimbursement.
Competitive pay: We're big on potential, and it's reflected in our competitive compensation packages and generous equity.
Complete support: Find flexible health plans at every premium level, and substantial subsidies that stand up to global standards.
Visibility is yours: You can count on direct exposure to our leadership team — we’re a team where good ideas travel quickly.
Paid global onsites: Magic happens IRL: we gather twice yearly to reconnect over shared meals or kayaking adventures. (We’ve visited Vail, San Diego, and Mexico City, to name a few.)
Impact is recognized: Growth opportunities follow your contributions, not rigid promotion timelines.
The Tilt Way
We're looking for people who chase excellence and impact. Those who stand behind their work, celebrating the wins and learning from the missteps equally. We foster an environment where every voice is valued and mutual respect is non-negotiable — brilliant jerks need not apply. We're in this together, working to expand access to fair credit and prove that people are incredible. When you join us, it's not just another day at the [virtual] office, you're helping millions of hardworking people reach better financial futures.
You’re pushing ahead in your career? We can get behind that. Join us in building the credit system that people deserve.

jobs.title: Head of Product, Credit Outcome
jobs.text:
ABOUT TIDE
At Tide, we help SMEs save time and money in the running of their businesses by not only offering business accounts and related banking services, but also a comprehensive set of highly usable and connected administrative solutions, from invoicing to accounting.
Tide is transforming the small business banking market and now supports over 2 million members globally across the UK, India, Germany and France.
Using advanced technology, all solutions are designed with SMEs in mind. With quick onboarding, low fees and innovative features, we thrive on making data driven decisions to serve our mission: to help SMEs save time and money so they can get back to doing what they love.
Tide facts:
Tide is available for UK, Indian, German and French SMEs
Over 2 million members globally and rapidly growing
Over $300 million raised in funding
3,000 Tideans globally
Recognised with Great Place to Work certification three years in a row, and among India’s Top 50 Best Workplaces in Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance in 2026
We have offices in Central London, with a member support and technology centre in Sofia, Bulgaria, technology centres in Serbia, Romania, Lithuania and Hyderabad and offices in Gurugram, New Delhi, Berlin, Paris and Luxembourg
ABOUT THE TEAM:
PCS helps small businesses find and take the right credit. The Credit Outcome vertical is the heaviest part of PCS: it owns the journey from a business's intent to a successful credit outcome, measured by our north-star metric, % 1st Outcome. It spans several markets and combines market-focused product teams (Scaled Markets, New Markets, India) with horizontal teams (Sales Engine and Platform). You will work hand in hand with a dedicated Engineering Director, Design, Product Operations, Analytics and Commercial Heads.
ABOUT THE ROLE:
Vision, strategy and outcomes
Own the vertical's north star: set the strategy and roadmap to grow % 1st Outcome, balancing margin, efficiency and member experience.
Place the big bets: prioritise across routing, human connection, integrations and decisioning (e.g. pre-qualification), and be explicit about what we will not do.
Regional focus: make sound trade-offs between markets, including scaling established markets and building new ones such as India.
Leadership and team growth
Lead and grow product leaders: hire, coach and develop Product Leads and Senior PMs, giving each a self-contained area of the business to own.
Clear ownership: ensure one accountable PM/EM pair per workstream, with no ambiguity on who owns what.
Operating rhythm: run planning, OKRs and reviews that connect team work to vertical and company goals.
Partnership and delivery
Engineering partnership: work as a true pair with the Engineering Director on roadmap, capacity and technical investment, including platform health.
Cross-functional influence: align Design, Data, Risk & Compliance, Commercial and Operations on priorities and launches.
Data and experimentation: use funnel analytics and experiments to find friction, make decisions and show impact in commercial terms.
Applied AI: identify where automation and AI (e.g. lead scoring, agentic sales tooling) can raise conversion and efficiency.
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR:
Experience: 8+ years in product management, with 3+ years leading product managers or product leads [TBC level/years].
Commercial acumen: you tie product decisions to revenue, margin and unit economics.
Data-native: comfortable with funnel analytics, experimentation and BI tools.
Technical fluency: you can engage confidently with engineers on APIs, integrations and data flows.
Leader of leaders: you coach strong PMs, set a high bar and create room for people to grow.
Influence without authority: you align senior stakeholders across functions and regions.
Nice to have: experience in lending, credit marketplaces, fintech or regulated financial services; experience building products in multiple markets, ideally including India.
WHAT YOU’LL GET IN RETURN:
Competitive Compensation - competitive salary and share options
Time Off – Generous annual leave on top of bank holidays.
Parental Leave – Paid maternity, paternity, and adoption leave to support your family journey.
Sabbatical – Extended unpaid and paid leave options after completing milestone years with Tide.
Health Insurance – Private family insurance with additional OPD coverage and top-up options.
Life & Accident Cover – Comprehensive accidental and life insurance protection.
Mental Wellbeing – Access to therapy sessions, courses, meditations, and workshops.
Volunteering & Development Days – Paid days annually for volunteering or personal growth.
Learning & Development – Annual budget for books, courses, coaching, and more.
WOO (Work Outside the Office) – Work from abroad for up to 90 days annually.
Home Office Setup – Contribution towards setting up your home office
Laptop Ownership – Keep your old laptop and get a new one when it’s time for a replacement.
Snacks & Meals – Office perks with snacks, coffee, tea, and lunch (location dependent).
TIDE IS A PLACE FOR EVERYONE
At Tide, we believe that we can only succeed if we let our differences enrich our culture. Our Tideans come from a variety of backgrounds and experience levels. We consider everyone irrespective of their ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, veteran, neurodiversity or differently-abled status. We celebrate diversity in our workforce as a cornerstone of our success. Our commitment to a broad spectrum of ideas and backgrounds is what enables us to build products that resonate with our members’ diverse needs and lives.
We are One Team and foster a transparent and inclusive environment, where everyone’s voice is heard.
At Tide, we thrive on diversity, embracing various backgrounds and experiences. We welcome all individuals regardless of ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, or disability. Our inclusive culture is key to our success, helping us build products that meet our members' diverse needs. We are One Team, committed to transparency and ensuring everyone’s voice is heard.
Disclaimer
It has come to our attention that individuals or agencies are falsely claiming to represent Tide and are reaching out to candidates regarding job opportunities. Please be aware that:
Tide does not charge any fees at any stage of the recruitment process.
All official Tide job opportunities are listed exclusively on our Careers Page and applications should be submitted through this channel.
Communication from Tide will only come from an official @tide.co email address.
Tide does not work with agencies or recruiters without prior formal engagement, and we do not authorize third parties to make job offers on our behalf.
If you are contacted by anyone misrepresenting Tide or requesting payment, please treat it as fraudulent and report it to us immediately at talent@tide.co
Your safety and trust are important to us, and we are committed to ensuring a fair and transparent recruitment process.
Tide leverages AI to enhance our hiring experience. You can read more about how we use AI in our recruitment process in our AI Policy.
Your personal data will be processed by Tide for recruitment purposes and in accordance with Tide's Recruitment Privacy Notice.

jobs.title: Vice President, Product Management (MDR)
jobs.text:
Vice President, Product Management (MDR)
Rapid7 is looking for a Vice President, Product Management to own the strategy, vision, and execution of our Managed Detection & Response (MDR) product portfolio. This is a rare opportunity to shape how thousands of organizations experience cybersecurity as a managed service, defining what great looks like at the intersection of human expertise and cutting-edge technology.
About the Team
Rapid7's MDR product team partners closely with our SOC, engineering, and go-to-market functions to shape the service experience, define platform capabilities, and continuously raise the bar on global managed security service delivery.
About the Role
As a Vice President, Product Management (MDR), your primary responsibility will be to set the product direction for Rapid7's managed security service while balancing customer needs, analyst capabilities, and strategic business goals. Specifically, your focus will be to:
Define and drive the MDR product strategy and roadmap, ensuring alignment with Rapid7's broader detection and response vision
Partner closely with SOC leadership to deeply understand analyst workflows, operational pain points, and necessary platform capabilities
Lead and develop a high-performing team of product managers, fostering accountability and continuous learning
Translate customer insights, market trends, and competitive intelligence into differentiated product decisions that drive retention and expansion
Collaborate with engineering to define and deliver a platform roadmap that gives MDR analysts speed, context, and automation
Serve as a senior customer-facing voice for the MDR product by engaging with strategic accounts and building trust through transparency
Define and track product OKRs and success metrics to continuously improve the service experience and business outcomes
Work cross-functionally with sales, marketing, and customer success to ensure product positioning, launch readiness, and customer adoption
The skills and qualities you'll bring include
Bring 12+ years of product management experience, with significant time spent leading product for managed services, SaaS platforms, or security products
Possess a deep understanding of the cybersecurity landscape, particularly in detection and response, MDR, SOC operations, or incident response
Demonstrate a proven track record of leading and scaling product teams in a fast-paced, customer-centric environment
Drive multi-year product vision through strategic doing while staying grounded in near-term execution and time-bound milestones
Establish clear accountability and ownership across teams to deliver value for managed service customers
Make efficient decisions that resolve complex product challenges and maintain operational momentum across functions
Communicate complex product strategies clearly to executive and customer audiences to foster commitment
Build global cross-functional networks across engineering, services, sales, and executive leadership to drive aligned business outcomes
Embrace challenging conversations constructively to find common ground across cross-functional stakeholder groups
Apply self-awareness to adapt leadership style to varying group dynamics across technical and business teams
Demonstrate an eager mindset toward navigating change by driving product evolution in a fast-moving market
Embody our core values to foster a culture of excellence that drives meaningful impact and collective success.
We know that the best ideas and solutions come from multi-dimensional teams. That’s because these teams reflect a variety of backgrounds and professional experiences. If you are excited about this role and feel your experience can make an impact, please don’t be shy - apply today.
About Rapid7
At Rapid7, our vision is to create a secure digital world for our customers, our industry, and our communities. We do this by harnessing our collective expertise and passion to challenge what’s possible and drive extraordinary impact. We’re building a dynamic and collaborative workplace where new ideas are welcome.
Protecting 11,500+ customers against bad actors and threats means we’re continuing to push the envelope just like we’ ve been doing for the past 20 years. If you ’re ready to solve some of the toughest challenges in cybersecurity, we’re ready to help you take command of your career. Join us.
Rapid7, Inc. is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. A candidate’s salary is determined by various factors including, but not limited to, relevant work experience, skills, and certifications. We evaluate compensation decisions on a case-by-case basis, and it is not typical for an individual to be hired at the very top of the salary range.
The annual salary range for this role, depending on location, is:
United States: $259,300.00 - 350,800.00 USD Annual
Salary ranges may vary based on geographical location. This range does not include variable/incentive compensation, equity and benefits (where applicable/eligible).
All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or any other status protected by applicable national, federal, state or local law.

jobs.title: Sr. Director, Technology Program Management
jobs.text:
FICO (NYSE: FICO)is a leading global analytics software company, helping businesses in 100+ countries make better decisions. Join our world-class team today and fulfill your career potential!
The Opportunity
FICO’s Global PMO is the function that keeps the company’s most critical enterprise programs on track, from strategic transformation initiatives to cross-functional platform investments. As Sr. Director, Technology Program Management, a senior leadership role within our Project Management discipline, you will build and lead the PMO’s technology program portfolio, ensuring critical initiatives land with speed, discipline, and measurable outcomes. This role reports into the VP of the Global PMO. The flagship program under this role is FICO’s Product and Engineering Transformation, moving the engineering organization to AI-native, service-oriented delivery at scale. In this new role, you’ll lead strategic oversight and portfolio governance while building the function alongside technology and product executives.
What You’ll Contribute
Own the Global PMO technology program portfolio, ensuring well-orchestrated delivery of key roadmap initiatives, establishing effective governance and prioritization frameworks, and bringing a predictable reporting cadence that gives leadership clear visibility into program health, risk, and investment performance across all active initiatives.
Serve as the executive escalation point for program-level decisions and cross-program conflicts, and champion AI-native, agile-at-scale program delivery by creating and evolving PMO methodologies, templates, and tooling, reducing ceremony and modeling the operating principles FICO is embedding across its engineering organization.
Provide senior sponsorship and strategic oversight for FICO’s flagship Product and Engineering Transformation program, rolling up the sleeves on implementation and partnering with executive sponsors across Product, Engineering, HR, Legal, and Security to align direction and resolve blockers requiring SVP-level engagement.
Hold the AI transformation team accountable to milestones, quality, and stakeholder outcomes, and represent program progress and risks in executive forums, translating complexity into clear business impact.
Act as a trusted partner to the Head of Product, Head of Engineering and Architecture, Head of Technology Operations, and other technology executives, providing the portfolio-level view needed to make investment and resourcing decisions.
Hire, develop, and retain a high-performing team of program managers, defining career paths, competency frameworks, and performance standards, while building a culture of accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement that earns the trust of engineering and product teams rather than adding bureaucratic overhead.
Drive and improve annual and quarterly technology program planning cycles, owning portfolio-level dashboards and executive reporting as the trusted source of truth on status, investment tracking, and outcomes.
Identify cross-program synergies, shared infrastructure needs, and resourcing conflicts early, and partner with Finance and HR to manage program budgets, headcount plans, and vendor relationships across the portfolio.
What We’re Seeking
Extensive, progressive experience in program and portfolio management specifically in product and engineering disciplines, including senior leadership experience overseeing technology programs in a complex enterprise environment.
Prior firsthand involvement in implementing and scaling AI-native or Agentic delivery frameworks and tooling.
Demonstrated success leading large-scale organizational and technology transformation programs, with a clear understanding of what enables them to succeed and what causes them to fail.
Strong executive presence and communication skills, with the ability to engage credibly with senior leadership, translate complexity into business impact, and influence without authority across a matrixed organization.
Experience building and leading high-performing PMO or program management teams, including hiring, developing, and retaining senior individual contributors and managers.
Deep understanding of software product and engineering organizations, including what slows delivery down and what governance models enable rather than impede progress.
Track record of building portfolio governance models that provide real oversight without adding bureaucratic drag.
Experience managing programs at the intersection of technology, organizational change, and business strategy simultaneously.
Familiarity with modern software delivery practices such as CI/CD, DevOps, and agile at scale is preferred, enabling credible assessment of program risk and engagement with engineering leaders.
Our Offer to You
An inclusive culture strongly reflecting our core values: Act Like an Owner, Delight Our Customers and Earn the Respect of Others.
The opportunity to make an impact and develop professionally by leveraging your unique strengths and participating in valuable learning experiences.
Highly competitive compensation, benefits and rewards programs that encourage you to bring your best every day and be recognized for doing so.
An engaging, people-first work environment offering work/life balance, employee resource groups, and social events to promote interaction and camaraderie.
The targeted base pay range for this role is: $150,500 to $236,500 with this range reflecting differences in candidate knowledge, skills and experience.
Why Make a Move to FICO?
At FICO, you can develop your career with a leading organization in one of the fastest-growing fields in technology today – Big Data analytics. You’ll play a part in our commitment to help businesses use data to improve every choice they make, using advances in artificial intelligence, machine learning, optimization, and much more.
FICO makes a real difference in the way businesses operate worldwide:
• Credit Scoring — FICO® Scores are used by 90 of the top 100 US lenders.
• Fraud Detection and Security — 4 billion payment cards globally are protected by FICO fraud systems.
• Lending — 3/4 of US mortgages are approved using the FICO Score.
Global trends toward digital transformation have created tremendous demand for FICO’s solutions, placing us among the world’s top 100 software companies by revenue. We help many of the world’s largest banks, insurers, retailers, telecommunications providers and other firms reach a new level of success. Our success is dependent on really talented people – just like you – who thrive on the collaboration and innovation that’s nurtured by a diverse and inclusive environment. We’ll provide the support you need, while ensuring you have the freedom to develop your skills and grow your career. Join FICO and help change the way business thinks!
Learn more about how you can fulfil your potential at
FICO promotes a culture of inclusion and seeks to attract a diverse set of candidates for each job opportunity. We are an equal employment opportunity employer and we’re proud to offer employment and advancement opportunities to all candidates without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, pregnancy, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. Research has shown that women and candidates from underrepresented communities may not apply for an opportunity if they don’t meet all stated qualifications. While our qualifications are clearly related to role success, each candidate’s profile is unique and strengths in certain skill and/or experience areas can be equally effective. If you believe you have many, but not necessarily all, of the stated qualifications we encourage you to apply.
Information submitted with your application is subject to the FICO Privacy policy at

jobs.title: Product Finance Director, R&D Capital Allocation & Engineering Operations
jobs.text:
(GAQ427R231)
About the role
As Databricks scales at unprecedented velocity, how we invest our R&D capital—both human and compute—is critical to our scale. We are looking for a Product Finance leader to own R&D capital allocation and engineering operations. You will be a key finance partner to our senior Engineering and Product Operations leaders, with a mandate that spans product-level R&D ROI, global workforce and location strategy, and the rapidly evolving economics of AI-enabled software development.
The impact you will have
Drive product-level ROI and R&D capital allocation
Establish frameworks to measure product-level ROI across a fast-moving platform like Databricks where engineering velocity is extremely high.
Operationalize ROI metrics so they directly inform product investment and resource allocation decisions.
Define engineering economics in the AI era
Partner with Engineering to model how AI developer tooling and internal token spend scale alongside headcount, quantifying the tradeoff between human capital and compute capital.
Measure the end-to-end cost of AI-enabled engineering, including the second-order impact on cloud spend, and partner with Engineering to optimize investments.
Shape global workforce and location strategy
Drive multi-year headcount planning across global engineering hubs, balancing cost per hire, talent density, and university recruiting pipelines.
Partner closely with Workplace and Facilities leadership to synchronize R&D hiring roadmaps with global real estate strategy and multi-year CapEx planning.
Scale R&D finance operations and build the team
Bring systems-level thinking to R&D finance operations, building scalable, automated workflows across headcount management, PO planning, monthly accruals, and SOX audit compliance.
Dogfood the Databricks platform to modernize internal finance tooling and deliver self-serve operational visibility to engineering leaders.
Build, mentor, and scale a high-performing team of finance professionals capable of operating seamlessly across strategic capital allocation and rigorous operational execution.
What we look for
Required
10+ years of experience in Strategic/Product Finance or R&D FP&A.
Deep experience managing large-scale R&D OpEx, headcount capacity modeling, and multi-site workforce planning within a high-growth enterprise software or cloud company.
A proven track record of partnering directly with senior Engineering, Product Operations, and People/Workplace executives to drive capital allocation and operational rigor.
Systems-level thinker with a demonstrated ability to re-engineer financial processes from scratch—spanning headcount tracking, procurement, close, and SOX controls—to support rapid scale.
Experience building, leading, and developing high-output finance teams in fast-moving environments.
Preferred
Direct experience analyzing cloud dev/test infrastructure and AI tooling/token costs.
Experience attributing shared engineering and platform R&D costs across a complex, multi-product portfolio to establish product-level profitability.
Hands-on proficiency with SQL, Python, or notebook environments (especially Databricks) to automate reporting and self-serve insights from large operational datasets.

The pay range(s) for this role is listed below and represents the expected salary range for non-commissionable roles or on-target earnings for commissionable roles. Actual compensation packages are based on several factors that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to job-related skills, depth of experience, relevant certifications and training, and specific work location. Based on the factors above, Databricks anticipates utilizing the full width of the range. The total compensation package for this position may also include eligibility for annual performance bonus, equity, and the benefits listed above.
