jobs.title: Chef de l'ingénierie | Head of Engineering
jobs.text:
ABOUT VALPAY
Founded in 2022, ValPay is an all-in-one payment solution tailored to empower its partners' software platforms. Designed for ambitious business owners wanting to focus on growing their business rather than the logistics needed to run it, ValPay helps companies prevent fraud, gain access to real-time reporting, and accept both online and in-person payments. ValPay's PayFac-as-a-Service model gives its partners all the benefits of integrated payments while handling the heavy lifting.
ValPay is a subsidiary of Valsoft.
THE ROLE
As Head of Engineering, you will own the engineering organization at ValPay — how it is structured, how it delivers, and how good it gets. You will report to the CEO and work alongside product and go-to-market leadership to turn a talented, lean team into a predictable, high-performing engineering function.
This is a build role, not a caretaker role. ValPay's engineering team has grown quickly and now needs someone to put real operating discipline behind it: a delivery rhythm people can count on, a management layer that holds, and technical standards that let the platform scale with the business — without losing the speed and hands-on energy that got ValPay here.
We are hiring for trajectory. This role is scoped as Head of Engineering today, and it is designed as the potential path to Chief Technology Officer at ValPay. We would rather hire someone with the ceiling to grow into that seat and back them properly than hire the title and hope. What earns the step up is straightforward: a delivery organization that runs without heroics, a leadership bench you built, and a track record of technical judgment the CEO and the board can lean on.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
Own engineering delivery end to end — planning, execution, release cadence, and quality — and make it predictable enough that the business can plan around it.
Build and lead the engineering management layer: hire, develop, and coach engineering managers, tech leads, and senior/staff engineers, and put a durable structure beneath you.
Partner with Product on roadmap feasibility, sequencing, and trade-offs. Product sets the what; you own the how and the when.
Set and enforce technical standards across the platform — architecture, code quality, testing, observability, and documentation — so the system scales as GMV and merchant count grow.
Serve as the senior technical escalation point for integrations with core payments partners (Adyen, Fiserv), working complex issues to resolution and feeding what you learn back into the platform.
Drive AI adoption inside engineering — in the SDLC, in developer productivity, and in the product where it measurably improves outcomes.
Own engineering operations and reliability: on-call, incident response, postmortems, and the SLAs a PCI DSS Level 1 payments platform has to hold.
Partner with security and compliance to keep PCI DSS certification and multi-jurisdiction obligations met as the platform expands.
Be a steady presence under pressure, and build the organizational muscle for the team to handle incidents increasingly without you.
WHAT YOU BRING
8+ years in software engineering, including 4+ years leading engineering teams, with at least some of that time managing managers or tech leads.
Proven experience building, structuring, and scaling technology organizations, ideally in high-growth environments.
Experience hiring and developing engineering leaders, and the appetite to keep doing it.
You can still apply hands-on technical depth, you review architecture, you can go deep in a design review or an incident, and engineers respect your judgment. You are not expected to write production code day to day.
Strong judgment on build-versus-buy, technical debt, and where to spend engineering capacity — and the ability to explain those calls in business terms to a non-technical executive team.
A track record of installing delivery process in a fast-moving team without killing its speed: planning cadence, release discipline, on-call, and the metrics to know whether it is working.
Demonstrable ambition and ceiling. You want the CTO seat eventually and you can show what you have been doing to get ready for it.
NICE TO HAVE
Payments, fintech, or other regulated/high-availability environments (PCI DSS, SOC 2, or similar).
Experience in a high-growth or private-equity-backed environment, or integrating engineering teams from acquisitions.
Experience with multi-tenant platform or API-first product architecture.
WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE
In the first six to twelve months:
A management layer is in place: engineering managers or tech leads owning their areas, with clear scope and accountability.
Engineering runs on a delivery rhythm the business can plan against — commitments are made and met, and slippage is visible early rather than at the deadline.
Delivery and reliability are measured, not felt — baseline metrics exist for throughput, lead time, change failure rate, and incident response, and they are trending the right way.
AI is in real use inside engineering, with live use cases rather than pilots.
On-call and incident response are defined and drilled, and incidents are increasingly resolved without you in the room.
Technical standards and architecture direction are written down, agreed, and actually followed.
WHY VALPAY

À PROPOS DE VALPAY
Fondée en 2022, ValPay est une solution de paiement tout-en-un conçue pour outiller les plateformes logicielles de ses partenaires. Pensée pour les entrepreneurs ambitieux qui souhaitent se consacrer à la croissance de leur entreprise plutôt qu'à la logistique nécessaire à son exploitation, ValPay aide les entreprises à prévenir la fraude, à accéder à des rapports en temps réel et à accepter les paiements en ligne comme en personne. Le modèle de facilitation des paiements en tant que service (PayFac-as-a-Service) de ValPay procure à ses partenaires tous les avantages des paiements intégrés, tout en prenant en charge le gros du travail.
ValPay est une filiale de Valsoft.
LE POSTE
À titre de chef de l'ingénierie, vous prendrez en charge l'organisation d'ingénierie de ValPay : sa structure, sa capacité de livraison et son niveau d'excellence. Vous relèverez du chef de la direction et travaillerez aux côtés des responsables du produit et de la mise en marché afin de transformer une équipe talentueuse et restreinte en une fonction d'ingénierie prévisible et très performante.
Il s'agit d'un rôle de bâtisseur, et non de gestionnaire de statu quo. L'équipe d'ingénierie de ValPay a connu une croissance rapide et a maintenant besoin d'une personne capable d'y instaurer une véritable discipline opérationnelle : une cadence de livraison fiable, une couche de gestion solide et des normes techniques permettant à la plateforme d'évoluer au rythme de l'entreprise — sans perdre la rapidité et l'énergie concrète qui ont mené ValPay jusqu'ici.
Nous recrutons pour le potentiel. Ce poste est défini aujourd'hui comme celui de chef de l'ingénierie, et il est conçu comme la voie d'accès possible au poste de chef de la technologie (CTO) chez ValPay. Nous préférons embaucher une personne ayant la capacité de croître vers ce rôle et l'appuyer pleinement, plutôt que d'embaucher un titre en espérant que cela fonctionne. Les conditions de cette progression sont claires : une organisation de livraison qui fonctionne sans héroïsme, un banc de leaders que vous aurez bâti, et un jugement technique sur lequel la direction et le conseil peuvent s'appuyer.
CE QUE VOUS FEREZ
Assumer la livraison en ingénierie de bout en bout — planification, exécution, cadence de mise en production et qualité — et la rendre suffisamment prévisible pour que l'entreprise puisse planifier en conséquence.
Bâtir et diriger la couche de gestion en ingénierie : embaucher, développer et encadrer des gestionnaires de l'ingénierie, des chefs techniques et des ingénieurs seniors ou principaux, et mettre en place une structure durable sous votre responsabilité.
Collaborer avec le Produit sur la faisabilité, le séquencement et les compromis de la feuille de route. Le Produit définit le quoi; vous êtes responsable du comment et du quand.
Définir et faire respecter les normes techniques de la plateforme — architecture, qualité du code, tests, observabilité et documentation — afin que le système évolue avec la croissance du volume de paiements et du nombre de marchands.
Agir comme point d'escalade technique senior pour les intégrations avec les principaux partenaires de paiement (Adyen, Fiserv), en menant les enjeux complexes jusqu'à leur résolution et en réinjectant les apprentissages dans la plateforme.
Piloter l'adoption de l'IA au sein de l'ingénierie — dans le cycle de développement, dans la productivité des développeurs et dans le produit lorsque les bénéfices sont mesurables.
Assumer les opérations d'ingénierie et la fiabilité : garde, réponse aux incidents, post-mortems et niveaux de service qu'exige une plateforme de paiement certifiée PCI DSS de niveau 1.
Collaborer avec les équipes de sécurité et de conformité afin de maintenir la certification PCI DSS et les obligations multijuridictionnelles à mesure que la plateforme s'étend.
Demeurer une présence stable sous pression et développer la capacité organisationnelle permettant à l'équipe de gérer les incidents de plus en plus sans vous.
CE QUE VOUS APPORTEZ
Au moins 8 ans d'expérience en génie logiciel, dont 4 ans ou plus à diriger des équipes d'ingénierie, incluant une période de gestion de gestionnaires ou de chefs techniques.
Expérience démontrée dans la création, la structuration et la mise à l'échelle d'organisations technologiques, idéalement dans des environnements à forte croissance.
Expérience d'embauche et de développement de leaders en ingénierie, et le désir de continuer à le faire.
Vous conservez une profondeur technique concrète et applicable : vous révisez l'architecture, vous pouvez approfondir une revue de conception ou un incident, et les ingénieurs respectent votre jugement. L'écriture de code en production au quotidien n'est pas attendue.
Un jugement solide sur les décisions de type « développer ou acheter », sur la dette technique et sur l'allocation de la capacité d'ingénierie — et la capacité d'expliquer ces choix en termes d'affaires à une équipe de direction non technique.
Un historique démontré d'implantation de processus de livraison dans une équipe qui avance vite, sans en freiner la rapidité : cadence de planification, discipline de mise en production, garde, et les indicateurs permettant d'en mesurer l'efficacité.
Une ambition et un potentiel démontrables. Vous visez éventuellement le poste de chef de la technologie et vous pouvez démontrer ce que vous faites pour vous y préparer.
ATOUTS RECHERCHÉS
Expérience dans les paiements, en technologie financière ou dans d'autres environnements réglementés à haute disponibilité (PCI DSS, SOC 2 ou équivalent).
Expérience dans un environnement à forte croissance ou détenu par un fonds d'investissement privé, ou en intégration d'équipes d'ingénierie issues d'acquisitions.
Expérience des architectures de plateforme multilocataire ou de produits axés sur les API.
CE À QUOI RESSEMBLE LA RÉUSSITE
Au cours des six à douze premiers mois :
Une couche de gestion est en place : des gestionnaires de l'ingénierie ou des chefs techniques responsables de leurs domaines, avec un périmètre et une imputabilité clairs.
L'ingénierie fonctionne selon une cadence de livraison sur laquelle l'entreprise peut planifier : les engagements sont pris et tenus, et les écarts sont visibles tôt plutôt qu'à l'échéance.
La livraison et la fiabilité sont mesurées, et non ressenties : des indicateurs de référence existent pour le débit, le délai de livraison, le taux d'échec des changements et la réponse aux incidents, et ils évoluent dans la bonne direction.
L'IA est utilisée concrètement au sein de l'ingénierie, avec des cas d'utilisation en production plutôt que des projets pilotes.
La garde et la réponse aux incidents sont définies et exercées, et les incidents se règlent de plus en plus sans votre présence.
Les normes techniques et l'orientation architecturale sont documentées, acceptées et réellement appliquées.
POURQUOI VALPAY
Fondée en 2022, ValPay fonctionne déjà à grande échelle : une plateforme certifiée PCI DSS de niveau 1, déployée dans plus de 40 territoires en Amérique du Nord, en Europe et en Asie-Pacifique, au service de plateformes logicielles verticales en dentisterie, en nautisme, en gestion immobilière, en automobile et ailleurs.
La croissance repose sur trois moteurs, qui s'appuient tous sur la même plateforme :
Ventes internes — convertir le volume de paiements (GMV) existant de Valsoft vers ValPay, une occasion de plus de 15 G$ dans la clientèle actuelle, à laquelle s'ajoute chaque nouvelle acquisition de Valsoft.
Canal des ISV externes — signer des ISV à l'extérieur du portefeuille de Valsoft, pour des revenus de 25 M$ à 50 M$, avec plus de 2 G$ d'ententes déjà conclues, maintenant converties en marchands actifs qui traitent des transactions.
Moteur d'acquisitions — acquérir des entreprises de passerelles de paiement : deux transactions conclues à ce jour, le même plan de conversion étant appliqué à chaque actif acquis.
Offrir des paiements intégrés au sein d'un portefeuille de plus de 150 sociétés de logiciels verticaux représente un réseau de distribution que la plupart des entreprises de paiement mettent des années à bâtir. ValPay le possède déjà. Ce qui déterminera la vitesse de ces trois moteurs, c'est l'organisation d'ingénierie qui les soutient — et c'est là le mandat de ce poste.
ValPay est soutenue par Valsoft, qui acquiert et conserve ses entreprises indéfiniment plutôt que de les revendre. Vous bâtissez sur un horizon long, et non en vue d'une sortie.
Pour en savoir plus : https://www.valpay.com/

blocks.text: ABOUT VALPAY

Founded in 2022, ValPay is an all-in-one payment solution tailored to empower its partners' software platforms. Designed for ambitious business owners wanting to focus on growing their business rather than the logistics needed to run it, ValPay helps companies prevent fraud, gain access to real-time reporting, and accept both online and in-person payments. ValPay's PayFac-as-a-Service model gives its partners all the benefits of integrated payments while handling the heavy lifting.
ValPay is a subsidiary of Valsoft.
THE ROLE

As Head of Engineering, you will own the engineering organization at ValPay — how it is structured, how it delivers, and how good it gets. You will report to the CEO and work alongside product and go-to-market leadership to turn a talented, lean team into a predictable, high-performing engineering function.

This is a build role, not a caretaker role. ValPay's engineering team has grown quickly and now needs someone to put real operating discipline behind it: a delivery rhythm people can count on, a management layer that holds, and technical standards that let the platform scale with the business — without losing the speed and hands-on energy that got ValPay here.

We are hiring for trajectory. This role is scoped as Head of Engineering today, and it is designed as the potential path to Chief Technology Officer at ValPay. We would rather hire someone with the ceiling to grow into that seat and back them properly than hire the title and hope. What earns the step up is straightforward: a delivery organization that runs without heroics, a leadership bench you built, and a track record of technical judgment the CEO and the board can lean on.
WHAT YOU'LL DO

items: Own engineering delivery end to end — planning, execution, release cadence, and quality — and make it predictable enough that the business can plan around it.
Build and lead the engineering management layer: hire, develop, and coach engineering managers, tech leads, and senior/staff engineers, and put a durable structure beneath you.
Partner with Product on roadmap feasibility, sequencing, and trade-offs. Product sets the what; you own the how and the when.
Set and enforce technical standards across the platform — architecture, code quality, testing, observability, and documentation — so the system scales as GMV and merchant count grow.
Serve as the senior technical escalation point for integrations with core payments partners (Adyen, Fiserv), working complex issues to resolution and feeding what you learn back into the platform.
Drive AI adoption inside engineering — in the SDLC, in developer productivity, and in the product where it measurably improves outcomes.
Own engineering operations and reliability: on-call, incident response, postmortems, and the SLAs a PCI DSS Level 1 payments platform has to hold.
Partner with security and compliance to keep PCI DSS certification and multi-jurisdiction obligations met as the platform expands.
Be a steady presence under pressure, and build the organizational muscle for the team to handle incidents increasingly without you.

blocks.text: WHAT YOU BRING

items: 8+ years in software engineering, including 4+ years leading engineering teams, with at least some of that time managing managers or tech leads.
Proven experience building, structuring, and scaling technology organizations, ideally in high-growth environments.
Experience hiring and developing engineering leaders, and the appetite to keep doing it.

You can still apply hands-on technical depth, you review architecture, you can go deep in a design review or an incident, and engineers respect your judgment. You are not expected to write production code day to day.
Strong judgment on build-versus-buy, technical debt, and where to spend engineering capacity — and the ability to explain those calls in business terms to a non-technical executive team.
A track record of installing delivery process in a fast-moving team without killing its speed: planning cadence, release discipline, on-call, and the metrics to know whether it is working.
Demonstrable ambition and ceiling. You want the CTO seat eventually and you can show what you have been doing to get ready for it.

blocks.text: NICE TO HAVE
Payments, fintech, or other regulated/high-availability environments (PCI DSS, SOC 2, or similar).
Experience in a high-growth or private-equity-backed environment, or integrating engineering teams from acquisitions.
Experience with multi-tenant platform or API-first product architecture.
WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE
In the first six to twelve months:

items: A management layer is in place: engineering managers or tech leads owning their areas, with clear scope and accountability.
Engineering runs on a delivery rhythm the business can plan against — commitments are made and met, and slippage is visible early rather than at the deadline.
Delivery and reliability are measured, not felt — baseline metrics exist for throughput, lead time, change failure rate, and incident response, and they are trending the right way.
AI is in real use inside engineering, with live use cases rather than pilots.
On-call and incident response are defined and drilled, and incidents are increasingly resolved without you in the room.
Technical standards and architecture direction are written down, agreed, and actually followed.

jobs.title: Head of Product
jobs.text:
Job Description | About the Role
The Product Manager ascertains what’s next for the product. Head of Product is a visionary who is also rich with applied experience. We’re looking for someone will work cross-functionally with engineering, growth, and marketing to bring unique value-based features to market across B2B2C.
This role moves at a fast pace while maintaining excellent quality and a positive working attitude to strategize the Fabulous product roadmap.
Expectations | Duties
Outreach and Data Accumulation
Connect with users: dig into user data, both qualitative and quantitative
Ascertains trends while being a champion for user-first experiences
Collaborate with researchers, data scientists, and business development teams to understand user needs and identify new product opportunities.
Immerse yourself in the psychology, pain points and behavior of users to develop strong intuition about solutions that will work for them.
Develop compelling roadmaps and metric targets that keep us on track towards our desired goals and continuously measure progress towards them.
Lead product ideation and prioritization within a key product area.
Evaluate ideas and lead product prioritization and releases
Have a consistent pipeline of fresh ideas that can help move the needle, through user research/feedback, driving brainstorms sessions, and doing competitive research
Ruthlessly prioritize these ideas in a robust, data-informed way, with an aim to have the most impact with limited resources – time, engineering resources, user volume, etc.
Leverage data to drive product development and experimentation.
Lead a cross-functional team through the product development cycle–UI/UX, engineering, QA, and data analysis.
Be the overall point-person to build compelling products and features for users.
Write design documents and web updates for new content/features/initiatives with input from curriculum, design & engineering partners.
Initiate data-driven experimentation and analysis on new products and features.
Requirements
Qualifications | Requirements
8+ years of relevant product management experience:
Experience in a prior startup or other high-ambiguity environment
Prior consumer-facing product development experience, ideally with mobile or subscription-based products
Prior experience with psychology-based products, gamification, or other user behavior-oriented apps
Additional PM skills we highly value:
Consumer user empathy & perspective
Driving strategy & big-picture thinking
Experience with data analysis, metrics, and goal-setting
Analytical dexterity a.k.a. critical problem solving
Scrappy–execution & outcome-focused
Curious and teachable
Benefits
About Us
An award-winning health, wellness, & coaching company that creates apps which fall the top ten internationally. Our science-based approach sits squarely in the tech-for-good lane, helping people live their best lives. Everyone who has joined this company is committed to using evidence-based research to find the absolute best ways to change lives for the better.
Our History
Three co-founders created the Fabulous app: Sami, Amine, and Taylor. Growing up in Tunisia, Sami and Amine were only 16 when they met. With their early iteration, they reached out to Taylor, an award-winning designer in Malaysia. Their vision was welcomed into an incubation lab for startups at Duke University led by world-renowned Behavioral Economics Professor Dan Ariely. Our Chief Storyteller Jaz co-founded the Introductory Psychology program at Stanford University.
Our Approach
We use a behavioral economics lens to help individuals find that 'on switch' inside them to achieve their fullest potential. What has emerged is a system that transforms tiny habits into profound long-term changes. A world in which people with ADHD thrive. A method for gratitude to reach through difficulty. A sanctuary to seek out your true purpose. A fountain of knowledge. A space for rest and self compassion.
Our Mission
Help every individual discover the wonderful person inside themselves by creating: beautiful, evidence-based, life-changing products.
Our Environment
The first thing that sets us apart is that we’re not a place at all. While we’re a remote company, it’s not unusual to feel you know your teammates better than those you’ve shared an office with in the past. Ours is a professionally nourishing environment that is flexible and fully remote. Team members enjoy in house challenges and Slack event and work across a variety of tools. Meetings are kept to a minimum and deep work is encouraged.
Our Awards
Apple Best Apps of 2018
Editor’s app choice in more than 30 countries
Winner of Google’s Material Design Award
Best App Finalist in Google Play Awards
Consistently ranking in the top ten Health & Fitness apps across platforms
Backed by Facebook Startup Lab and Microsoft Venture
Our Norms
Ownership: Be the CEO of your tasks. No one is watching over your shoulder. Be the proof.

About Us

An award-winning health, wellness, & coaching company that creates apps which fall the top ten internationally. Our science-based approach sits squarely in the tech-for-good lane, helping people live their best lives. Everyone who has joined this company is committed to using evidence-based research to find the absolute best ways to change lives for the better.
Our History

Three co-founders created the Fabulous app: Sami, Amine, and Taylor. Growing up in Tunisia, Sami and Amine were only 16 when they met. With their early iteration, they reached out to Taylor, an award-winning designer in Malaysia. Their vision was welcomed into an incubation lab for startups at Duke University led by world-renowned Behavioral Economics Professor Dan Ariely. Our Chief Storyteller Jaz co-founded the Introductory Psychology program at Stanford University.

What has emerged is a system that transforms tiny habits into profound long-term changes. A world in which people with ADHD thrive. A method for gratitude to reach through difficulty. A sanctuary to seek out your true purpose. A fountain of knowledge. A space for rest and self compassion.
Our Mission
Help every individual discover the wonderful person inside themselves by creating: beautiful, evidence-based, life-changing products.

While we’re a remote company, it’s not unusual to feel you know your teammates better than those you’ve shared an office with in the past. Ours is a professionally nourishing environment that is flexible and fully remote. Team members enjoy in house challenges and Slack event and work across a variety of tools. Meetings are kept to a minimum and deep work is encouraged.

Editor’s app choice in more than 30 countries
Winner of Google’s Material Design Award
Best App Finalist in Google Play Awards
Consistently ranking in the top ten Health & Fitness apps across platforms
Backed by Facebook Startup Lab and Microsoft Venture

jobs.text:
Job Title: VP, Product Delivery & Growth - AI
Location: USA - Remote
**Travel to Office expectations**
For Remote Roles: If this role is remote, there will be in-office events that will require travel to and from the Mississauga and/or Salt Lake City office. These will include, but not limited to, onboarding, team events, semi-annual and annual team meetings.
At PointClickCare our mission is simple: to help providers deliver exceptional care. And that starts with our people. As a leading health tech company that’s founder-led and privately held, we empower our employees to push boundaries, innovate, and shape the future of healthcare.
With the largest long-term and post-acute care dataset and a Marketplace of 400+ integrated partners, our platform serves over 30,000 provider organizations, making a real difference in millions of lives. We also reinvest a significant percentage of our revenue back into research and development, ensuring our employees have the resources to innovate and make a lasting impact. Recognized by Forbes as a top private cloud company and honored as one of Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, we offer flexibility, growth opportunities, and meaningful work.
At PointClickCare, we empower our people to be the architects of a smarter healthcare future; one that is human-first and accelerated by AI to create meaningful and lasting change. Employees harness AI as a catalyst for creativity, productivity, and thoughtful decision-making. By integrating AI tools into our daily workflows, collaboration is enhanced, outcomes are improved, and every team member has the proficiency to maximize their impact. It all starts with our hiring practices where we uncover AI expertise that complements our mission, and we continue to invest in training and development to nurture innovation throughout the employee journey.
Join us in redefining healthcare , so it doesn’t just survive, it thrives. To learn more about PointClickCare, check out Life at PointClickCare and connect with us on Glassdoor and LinkedIn.
About the Team
The Integrated Care + SNF Reimbursement portfolio spans the connected workflows that carry a resident from referral through care delivery to payment: including, acute and payer care collaboration on the National Care Collaboration Network and Audacious platforms, Secure Conversations across our customer segments, practitioner EHR solutions, SNF admissions and managed care workflows, and SNF revenue cycle and reimbursement optimization.
The Outbound Product Management team within this portfolio is the bridge between strategic customer relationships, go-to-market execution, and product direction. The team is remote and hybrid across the US and Canada, and works shoulder to shoulder with inbound Product Management, Engineering, and every GTM function.
Key Responsibilities:
Go-To-Market Strategy & Portfolio Growth: Own end-to-end go-to-market strategy for the portfolio from launch through scale. Define the growth thesis for each product line, set adoption and revenue targets with Sales and Revenue Operations, and drive cross-functional accountability for attainment.
Commercial Model & Monetization: Lead pricing, packaging, and monetization strategy for new and AI-enabled capabilities, including usage-based pricing, tiered access, and enterprise licensing. Partner with Pricing, Finance, and Revenue Operations on scalable models that protect margin.
Product Strategy & Roadmap: Partner with inbound Product Management leaders to shape portfolio direction, translating customer feedback, competitive signals, and adoption data into roadmap and investment recommendations. Serve as the commercial voice in portfolio planning and trade-off decisions.
Executive Customer Engagement & Market Leadership: Build executive relationships across strategic SNF, payer, practitioner, and acute accounts. Lead beta and co-development programs that generate real-world proof points, and represent PointClickCare with customers, industry bodies, and analysts.
Organizational Leadership & Talent Development: Lead and grow the Outbound Product Management function, including leaders of teams. Hire, coach, and develop talent, establish operating cadence and standards aligned with the product development lifecycle and go-to-market model, and foster accountability, inclusion, and continuous improvement.
Portfolio Performance & Market Insight: Define and track portfolio, customer engagement, and go-to-market KPIs. Lead competitive analysis, customer research, and thought leadership, and partner with legal, compliance, and governance teams to support responsible deployment of AI-enabled capabilities.

Hire, coach, and develop talent, establish operating cadence and standards aligned with the product development lifecycle and go-to-market model, and foster accountability, inclusion, and continuous improvement.
Portfolio Performance & Market Insight: Define and track portfolio, customer engagement, and go-to-market KPIs. Lead competitive analysis, customer research, and thought leadership, and partner with legal, compliance, and governance teams to support responsible deployment of AI-enabled capabilities.
Required Skills & Qualifications:
12+ years of experience in product management, product marketing, or product growth, including 5+ years leading teams at the Director level or above.
Demonstrated ownership of go-to-market strategy for a multi-product portfolio, with accountability for adoption and revenue outcomes beyond launch execution.
Proven success building commercial models for SaaS and AI-enabled products, including pricing, packaging, and monetization, with fluency in ARR, NRR, CAC, LTV, and churn.
Executive presence and demonstrated ability to influence and align senior leaders across Sales, Sales Enablement, Customer Success, Revenue Operations, Solutions, Pricing, and Professional Services.
Experience leading leaders, including hiring, developing, and scaling teams through organizational change.
Strong data-driven decision-making skills, using qualitative and quantitative signals to set priorities and make defensible trade-offs.
Ability to travel regularly to strategic customer sites and industry events, with occasional travel to PointClickCare offices.
Preferred Experience:
Background in post-acute care, senior care, or payer-provider collaboration models.
Experience taking AI-enabled products to market, including generative AI, large language model, and agentic capabilities.
Familiarity with interoperability, care transitions, and referral and authorization workflows.

Our salary ranges are determined by job and level. jobs.title: Director of Product
jobs.text:
Real people. Real service.
At SupplyHouse.com, we value every individual team member and cultivate a community where people come first. Led by our core values of Generosity, Respect, Innovation, Teamwork, and GRIT, we’re dedicated to maintaining a supportive work environment that celebrates diversity and empowers everyone to reach their full potential. As an industry-leading e-commerce company specializing in HVAC, plumbing, heating, and electrical supplies since 2004, we strive to foster growth while providing the best possible experience for our customers.
We are looking for a Director of Product to own our product operating model end to end: the practice of product management, the delivery engine that gets work shipped, and the annual roadmap that connects both to company strategy. Reporting into our COO, this individual will lead a team of Product Managers embedded in cross-functional pods and hold those pods accountable for measurable customer and business outcomes. The Director of Product will work in close partnership with the VP of IT, Senior Manager of UX, Director of Enterprise AI Adoption, and business leaders to connect customer needs, business priorities, technical strategy, and execution. If you’re passionate about building high-performing product organizations, enjoy turning strategy into action, and are excited to lead cross-functional teams in delivering product experiences that are strategically sound, technically feasible, thoughtfully designed, and impactful for customers and the business, we want to hear from you!
This remote position is open to individuals who live in, or are open to relocating to, the following states: Arizona, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Nevada, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Rhode Island, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, and Washington.
This position requires travel to our headquarters in Melville, NY 6 times per year for internal meetings and team building activities. We reimburse reasonable and necessary travel expenses, and you’re also welcome to work on-site anytime beyond these visits – our doors are always open.
Role Type: Full-Time, Exempt
Location: Remote
Schedule: Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. with time zone flexibility
Base Salary: The expected starting salary for the position is $193,389 to $276,270 within a full position range of $193,389 to $359,151 annually. This range reflects the long-term earning potential for the role. Our starting pay practice is the minimum to middle portion of the range, depending on experience, qualifications, and internal equity, consistent with applicable law and it is rare for a new hire to start above the midpoint.
What you will own:
Accountability across the pod structure
Pod ownership. Own outcome accountability for every product pod, ensuring each has a clear mission, a primary success metric, and explicit guardrail metrics.
Decision rights and shared accountability. Establish clear decision rights across Product, UX, and Engineering. Product leads customer problem definition, business outcomes, prioritization, and roadmap decisions; UX leads research and experience design; Engineering leads technical architecture and implementation. Hold each trio jointly accountable for delivering measurable outcomes, with unresolved tradeoffs escalated and decided quickly.
Cross-pod seams. Resolve cross-pod dependencies, sequencing conflicts, and platform-versus-feature tradeoffs before they become delivery risk.
Operating cadence. Define and maintain the standards that make pods legible to leadership: how bets are written, how success is defined up front, how results get reported, and what happens when we need to pivot.
Leading and developing product managers
People leadership. Directly manage and coach a team of product managers with clear leveling expectations and honest, specific feedback.
Craft development. Build Product Management craft across discovery and delivery: opportunity framing, jobs-to-be-done and customer problem definition, hypothesis writing, experiment design, and evidence-based prioritization.
Hiring. Recruit, onboard, and retain strong product talent. Own the hiring bar and the interview loop for the function.
Influence without authority. Coach Product Managers to lead through influence across Merchandising, Marketing, Operations, Customer Service, and Engineering without relying on formal authority.
Managing to outcomes, not outputs
Outcome definition. Translate company strategy into a product strategy with a north star metric and a supporting metric tree, so every pod can trace its work to a business result.
Measurement. Replace feature-count reporting with outcome reporting: leading and lagging indicators, target versus actual, and a clear read on what we learned.
Continuous discovery. Partner with the Director of Customer Experience to establish a consistent customer research and usability practice across product teams, validate bets before they consume significant engineering capacity, and stop or pivot work that is not moving the intended metric.
Evidence-based prioritization. Ensure prioritization reflects qualitative customer insight, behavioral data, business performance, and operational feedback rather than stakeholder preference alone.
Customer proximity. Build direct exposure to professional tradespeople and internal users into the product management operating model.
Portfolio balance. Manage capacity as a portfolio of bets across core growth, platform health, and exploratory work, and be able to defend that allocation to the executive team.
Roadmap ownership
Annual roadmap. Build and publish the annual product roadmap, then maintain it as a living now / next / later view rather than a fixed feature calendar with dates attached to everything.
Quarterly planning. Run the quarterly planning process: OKR setting, bet selection, capacity modeling, and tradeoff decisions with clear rationale.
Executive alignment. Keep the roadmap credible with senior leadership and the board through clear, unhedged communication about what is committed, what is a bet, and what changed.
Backlog health. Maintain a rigorously prioritized backlog with a real definition of ready and definition of done, so pods are never blocked on ambiguity.
Project management and delivery
Integrated planning. Ensure significant initiatives have clear scope, milestones, owners, dependencies, resource assumptions, risks, decision points, and launch criteria.
Risk management. Establish a consistent process for identifying, escalating, and resolving delivery risks before they affect committed outcomes or timelines.
Delivery accountability. Hold product managers accountable for maintaining clear plans, decisions, status reporting, and stakeholder alignment from discovery through post-launch evaluation.
Cross-functional execution. Coordinate dependencies across Product, IT, UX, AI Enterprise Enablement, Marketing, Merchandising, Operations, Customer Service, and other impacted teams.
Commitment discipline. Differentiate committed work from discovery, experiments, and potential future investments so leadership has an accurate view of delivery confidence.
Change management and adoption. Ensure significant product launches include stakeholder communication, training, operational readiness, adoption planning, and feedback mechanisms. Hold product teams accountable for sustained adoption and value realization, not only technical release.
Post-launch accountability. Require adoption, performance, customer feedback, operational impact, and lessons learned to be reviewed after launch.
Delivery health. Measure and improve delivery health through indicators such as cycle time, throughput, and predictability.
Process stewardship. Improve the tools and operating rhythms that make delivery visible, while removing process that does not improve decisions, accountability, or execution.
Technical product leadership
Partner with the VP of IT and engineering leaders to align the product roadmap with technical strategy, architecture, capacity, security, reliability, scalability, and platform health.
Ensure product managers can translate business and customer needs into requirements that account for system dependencies, integrations, data flows, APIs, and nonfunctional requirements.
Evaluate build, buy, and partner options using customer value, business impact, technical feasibility, implementation risk, total cost, and long-term maintainability.
Balance customer-facing enhancements with platform modernization, technical debt reduction, system reliability, and foundational capabilities.
Ensure technical constraints and dependencies are surfaced early enough to inform prioritization, sequencing, and executive decisions.
Establish strong partnership between product managers and technical leads without expecting product managers to dictate engineering solutions.
AI-enabled product strategy
Partner closely with the Director of AI Enterprise Enablement to identify, evaluate, and prioritize AI opportunities across customer-facing products and internal workflows.
Translate validated AI opportunities into product roadmaps with clear users, business outcomes, success measures, data requirements, and adoption plans.
Ensure AI-enabled product decisions consider usability, data quality, security, responsible-use expectations, technical feasibility, and ongoing performance.
Distinguish between experimentation and scalable production capabilities, with clear criteria for piloting, measuring, expanding, or discontinuing AI solutions.
Promote reuse of enterprise AI capabilities and prevent fragmented tools or duplicative solutions from developing across product teams.
Data and analytics

blocks.text: Real people. Real service.

At SupplyHouse.com, we value every individual team member and cultivate a community where people come first. Led by our core values of Generosity, Respect, Innovation, Teamwork, and GRIT, we’re dedicated to maintaining a supportive work environment that celebrates diversity and empowers everyone to reach their full potential. As an industry-leading e-commerce company specializing in HVAC, plumbing, heating, and electrical supplies since 2004, we strive to foster growth while providing the best possible experience for our customers.

We are looking for a Director of Product to own our product operating model end to end: the practice of product management, the delivery engine that gets work shipped, and the annual roadmap that connects both to company strategy. Reporting into our COO, this individual will lead a team of Product Managers embedded in cross-functional pods and hold those pods accountable for measurable customer and business outcomes. The Director of Product will work in close partnership with the VP of IT, Senior Manager of UX, Director of Enterprise AI Adoption, and business leaders to connect customer needs, business priorities, technical strategy, and execution. If you’re passionate about building high-performing product organizations, enjoy turning strategy into action, and are excited to lead cross-functional teams in delivering product experiences that are strategically sound, technically feasible, thoughtfully designed, and impactful for customers and the business, we want to hear from you!

This remote position is open to individuals who live in, or are open to relocating to, the following states: Arizona, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Nevada, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Rhode Island, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, and Washington.

This position requires travel to our headquarters in Melville, NY 6 times per year for internal meetings and team building activities. We reimburse reasonable and necessary travel expenses, and you’re also welcome to work on-site anytime beyond these visits – our doors are always open.
Role Type: Full-Time, Exempt
Location: Remote
Schedule: Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. with time zone flexibility

Base Salary: The expected starting salary for the position is $193,389 to $276,270 within a full position range of $193,389 to $359,151 annually. This range reflects the long-term earning potential for the role. Our starting pay practice is the minimum to middle portion of the range, depending on experience, qualifications, and internal equity, consistent with applicable law and it is rare for a new hire to start above the midpoint.
What you will own:
Accountability across the pod structure

items: Pod ownership. Own outcome accountability for every product pod, ensuring each has a clear mission, a primary success metric, and explicit guardrail metrics.

Decision rights and shared accountability. Establish clear decision rights across Product, UX, and Engineering. Product leads customer problem definition, business outcomes, prioritization, and roadmap decisions; UX leads research and experience design; Engineering leads technical architecture and implementation. Hold each trio jointly accountable for delivering measurable outcomes, with unresolved tradeoffs escalated and decided quickly.
Cross-pod seams. Resolve cross-pod dependencies, sequencing conflicts, and platform-versus-feature tradeoffs before they become delivery risk.

Operating cadence. Define and maintain the standards that make pods legible to leadership: how bets are written, how success is defined up front, how results get reported, and what happens when we need to pivot.

blocks.text: Leading and developing product managers

items: People leadership. Directly manage and coach a team of product managers with clear leveling expectations and honest, specific feedback.

Craft development. Build Product Management craft across discovery and delivery: opportunity framing, jobs-to-be-done and customer problem definition, hypothesis writing, experiment design, and evidence-based prioritization.
Hiring. Recruit, onboard, and retain strong product talent. Own the hiring bar and the interview loop for the function.
Influence without authority. Coach Product Managers to lead through influence across Merchandising, Marketing, Operations, Customer Service, and Engineering without relying on formal authority.

blocks.text: Managing to outcomes, not outputs

items: Outcome definition. Translate company strategy into a product strategy with a north star metric and a supporting metric tree, so every pod can trace its work to a business result.
Measurement. Replace feature-count reporting with outcome reporting: leading and lagging indicators, target versus actual, and a clear read on what we learned.

Continuous discovery. Partner with the Director of Customer Experience to establish a consistent customer research and usability practice across product teams, validate bets before they consume significant engineering capacity, and stop or pivot work that is not moving the intended metric.
Evidence-based prioritization. Ensure prioritization reflects qualitative customer insight, behavioral data, business performance, and operational feedback rather than stakeholder preference alone.
Customer proximity. Build direct exposure to professional tradespeople and internal users into the product management operating model.
Portfolio balance. Manage capacity as a portfolio of bets across core growth, platform health, and exploratory work, and be able to defend that allocation to the executive team.

blocks.text: Roadmap ownership

items: Annual roadmap. Build and publish the annual product roadmap, then maintain it as a living now / next / later view rather than a fixed feature calendar with dates attached to everything.
Quarterly planning. Run the quarterly planning process: OKR setting, bet selection, capacity modeling, and tradeoff decisions with clear rationale.
Executive alignment. Keep the roadmap credible with senior leadership and the board through clear, unhedged communication about what is committed, what is a bet, and what changed.
Backlog health. Maintain a rigorously prioritized backlog with a real definition of ready and definition of done, so pods are never blocked on ambiguity.

blocks.text: Project management and delivery

items: Integrated planning. Ensure significant initiatives have clear scope, milestones, owners, dependencies, resource assumptions, risks, decision points, and launch criteria.
Risk management. Establish a consistent process for identifying, escalating, and resolving delivery risks before they affect committed outcomes or timelines.
Delivery accountability. Hold product managers accountable for maintaining clear plans, decisions, status reporting, and stakeholder alignment from discovery through post-launch evaluation.
Cross-functional execution. Coordinate dependencies across Product, IT, UX, AI Enterprise Enablement, Marketing, Merchandising, Operations, Customer Service, and other impacted teams.
Commitment discipline. Differentiate committed work from discovery, experiments, and potential future investments so leadership has an accurate view of delivery confidence.

Change management and adoption. Ensure significant product launches include stakeholder communication, training, operational readiness, adoption planning, and feedback mechanisms. Hold product teams accountable for sustained adoption and value realization, not only technical release.
Post-launch accountability. Require adoption, performance, customer feedback, operational impact, and lessons learned to be reviewed after launch.
Delivery health. Measure and improve delivery health through indicators such as cycle time, throughput, and predictability.
Process stewardship. Improve the tools and operating rhythms that make delivery visible, while removing process that does not improve decisions, accountability, or execution.

blocks.text: Technical product leadership

items: Partner with the VP of IT and engineering leaders to align the product roadmap with technical strategy, architecture, capacity, security, reliability, scalability, and platform health.
Ensure product managers can translate business and customer needs into requirements that account for system dependencies, integrations, data flows, APIs, and nonfunctional requirements.
Evaluate build, buy, and partner options using customer value, business impact, technical feasibility, implementation risk, total cost, and long-term maintainability.
Balance customer-facing enhancements with platform modernization, technical debt reduction, system reliability, and foundational capabilities.
Ensure technical constraints and dependencies are surfaced early enough to inform prioritization, sequencing, and executive decisions.
Establish strong partnership between product managers and technical leads without expecting product managers to dictate engineering solutions.

items: Partner closely with the Director of AI Enterprise Enablement to identify, evaluate, and prioritize AI opportunities across customer-facing products and internal workflows.
Translate validated AI opportunities into product roadmaps with clear users, business outcomes, success measures, data requirements, and adoption plans.
Ensure AI-enabled product decisions consider usability, data quality, security, responsible-use expectations, technical feasibility, and ongoing performance.
Distinguish between experimentation and scalable production capabilities, with clear criteria for piloting, measuring, expanding, or discontinuing AI solutions.
Promote reuse of enterprise AI capabilities and prevent fragmented tools or duplicative solutions from developing across product teams.

jobs.title: Director Engineering, Adtech & Marketplace
jobs.text:
About your tasks:
Shape Retail Media & Marketplace: Set the engineering direction across both domains, deciding where the platforms should converge to create the most value for brands, sellers and Redcare.
Lead and grow the organisation: Develop your Engineering Managers and their teams, shaping the organisation as the domains evolve while creating an environment with clear ownership and autonomy.
Drive engineering excellence: Own delivery, reliability, architecture and technical debt, continuously raising engineering maturity and enabling teams to move quickly without compromising quality.
Turn technology into commercial impact: Co-own roadmaps with Product and Commercial, connecting engineering priorities to outcomes such as take rate, advertiser ROAS, seller economics and contribution margin.
Own strategic partnerships: Lead engineering relationships with external platforms, integrators and agencies, including build/buy/partner decisions, integrations, SLAs and vendor performance.
About you:
You have 3+ years of experience leading multiple engineering teams through managers or leads and have successfully led organisations through significant change, such as merging domains, introducing new scope or replacing a platform.
You have led development of commercial B2B platforms such as a marketplace, retail media, ad tech, payments or a seller/partner platform, with experience across high-traffic and transactional systems.
You combine strong technical judgement with commercial thinking, connecting engineering decisions to business outcomes and confidently partnering with senior Product and Commercial stakeholders.
You care deeply about engineering excellence, can demonstrate measurable improvements you have driven, and are comfortable navigating ambiguity, external partners and competing priorities. Strong English communication skills are essential.
About your benefits:
In order to provide you with the best possible support for your individual needs - whether it‘s living a healthy life, having enough time for your family, or developing your skills - we offer a wide range of different, site-specific benefits:
Sports: Stay healthy. Profit from a membership (M) package at Urban Sports Club, so that you can take advantage of a huge variety of sport offers.
Work from Home: If your job does not require you to be present in the office, we can arrange the place you work from individually - even for up to 20 days a year anywhere in the EU.
Personal development: Grow! We support and encourage your individual development through various in- and external trainings.
Vacation: 30 days paid vacation per annum (plus another day on Rosenmontag) and the option to take unpaid vacation of up to 10 days (after one year working with us).
Corporate pension plan: We offer a company pension scheme and have a dedicated external consultant to offer you the best guidance and advice.
About Redcare Pharmacy:
As Europe’s No.1 e-pharmacy Redcare Pharmacy is powered by passionate teams and cutting-edge innovation. We strive to create a healthy collaborative work environment where every employee feels valued and inspired to contribute to our vision “Until every human has their health”. If you’re seeking a career that offers purpose and aligns with your values join us and start your #Redcareer today.
About the role:
Retail Media and Marketplace are two of Redcare Pharmacy’s fastest-growing and most strategically important domains — and this is your opportunity to shape how they evolve together. Leading an engineering organisation of around 40 engineers across 5–7 teams, you will decide where these two distinct platforms should converge to create a seamless experience for brands and sellers, and where they should remain separate to perform at their best.
This is a high-visibility leadership role where your decisions will directly influence our customer experience and commercial growth. Reporting to our Executive Director of Engineering / VP of Engineering, you will lead through two Engineering Managers and partner closely with Product and Commercial leadership to turn engineering strategy into measurable business outcomes.

jobs.title: Director – Forward Deployed Engineering
jobs.text:
About Re:Build
At Re:Build, our mission is to ensure the next generation of important products are made, at scale, in America. We are laying the foundation for a better future for our customers, employees, and communities by revitalizing America's manufacturing base and creating meaningful jobs across the country, including in historically deindustrialized regions.
We operate an advanced, end-to-end manufacturing platform that partners with industrial companies and innovators to take products from first concept to full-scale production in critical verticals including aerospace and defense, electrification, medical, energy and environment, and robotics and automation.
The way we operate is as important as the work we do. It's guided by The Re:Build Way, 16 principles that shape how we collaborate with each other, partner with our customers and vendors, and contribute to the communities where we operate. (link to The Re:Build Way principles)
Who we are looking for
The Director, Forward Deployed Engineering is a hands-on leadership role in Re:Build Manufacturing's Digital Innovation Group (DIG). This role reflects the organization’s belief that digital innovation is key to scaling as a premier industrial company. In this position, the Director is responsible for hiring, leading, and developing a team of Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) who are embedded across Re:Build sites and Resource Center functions, implementing full-stack digital solutions that solve real-world business problems and drive measurable business impact. Success in the role depends on the ability to build trust, ensure alignment, and partner effectively with internal stakeholders throughout the entire product lifecycle. The ideal candidate combines a strong software engineering background with proven experience managing software delivery and solution engineering that directly serves customers. They bring deep technical credibility, strong people leadership skills, and the judgment needed to keep engagements well prioritized and delivered quickly.
What you get to do
Partner with portfolio Manufacturing, Engineering Services, and Functional teams to identify difficulties, operational inefficiencies, and opportunities for digital solutions
Evaluate and prioritize digital solution opportunities based on business impact, feasibility, and strategic alignment
Guide FDEs through sophisticated technical decisions, feature development, fixing issues, code reviews, and delivery execution across collaborator engagement
Define and implement engineering standards and coding practices across FDE projects to ensure scalability, maintainability, and security of delivered solutions
Build the repeatable delivery machine of reusable assets, playbooks, user documentation, and implementation approaches that strengthen delivery excellence and collaborator enablement
Establish metrics to measure solution impact and value post-deployment and gather feedback for continuous improvement
Evaluate and foster the adoption of emerging AI-assisted development tools (e.g., code generation, review, testing automation) across the FDE team to accelerate delivery velocity and code quality
Know the latest digital trends in AI, software development, manufacturing, Industry 4.0 technologies, and relevant SaaS solutions
Ability to travel 25% to customer sites (will only require domestic US travel)
What you bring to the Team
Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or related field required; MBA or relevant advanced degree; or equivalent combination of education and experience preferred
8+ years of experience leading customer-facing software delivery, implementation, solution engineering, consulting, or technical delivery programs within enterprise SaaS, technology, or systems integrator environments
2+ years of people leadership or technical leadership experience leading and developing engineers, architects, consultants, or technical delivery teams
3-5 years of hands-on software development, solution engineering, integration development, or full-stack development experience, including technical leadership responsibilities
Experience with DevSecOps practices, secure software development lifecycle (SDLC) methodologies, and Agile/SAFe delivery frameworks
Fluency in AI technologies applied to software development lifecycle
Proficiency with project and delivery management tools such as Jira and Confluence, with a proven ability to lead cross-functional teams and multiple concurrent engagements
Experience in manufacturing operations, industrial engineering, or engineering services strongly preferred
The BIG payoff
We are a company who is going to make a difference in the industries and the communities in which we choose to operate. Every employee of Re:Build will share ownership in the company and will share in the financial rewards of the success we achieve together, at all levels of the company!
We want to work with people that reflect the communities in which we operate
Re:Build Manufacturing is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status, marital status, parental status, cultural background, organizational level, work styles, tenure and life experiences. Or for any other reason.
Re:Build is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities in our job application procedures. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, you may contact us at or you may call us at 617.909.6275.

jobs.title: Head of Product
jobs.text:
About the Role:
We are hiring a hands-on Head of Product to own product direction, roadmap, feature definition, acceptance, and customer enablement. You will work closely with the Head of Engineering to take customer problems through discovery, delivery, and adoption, using AI to help a small team achieve exceptional speed and quality. You will be expected to produce specifications and prototypes, test workflows, and assess product results directly.
What You Will Own:
Set product direction, priorities, and scope within agreed business goals and budget.
Translate customer needs into complete workflows, clear specifications, acceptance criteria, and measurable success outcomes.
Use AI for research synthesis, prototyping, feature definition, product documentation, and acceptance work.
Own usability and product acceptance, including error and permission states, onboarding, guidance, and adoption.
Resolve scope and delivery trade-offs with Engineering and communicate progress through demonstrated customer outcomes.
Continuously evaluate the product, identify gaps, and turn customer feedback into actionable product improvements.
What You Bring
Proven experience taking commerce, SaaS, marketplace, or operational products from customer problems through to shipped and adopted workflows.
Strong discovery, prioritization, specification, and product measurement skills, with clear examples of product trade-offs you've made.
Hands-on AI proficiency, with the ability to personally produce and evaluate useful prototypes, specifications, workflows, and acceptance materials.
Strong critical-thinking skills and the ability to challenge assumptions, test products thoroughly, and distinguish activity from genuine customer value.
Experience working closely with Engineering and the ability to operate independently within a small, fast-moving team.
Strong understanding of user experience, onboarding, product adoption, and workflow design.
AI-Assisted Product Work
AI-assisted product work is mandatory. You must be able to demonstrate how you use AI to improve your speed, quality, research, prototyping, and product output while retaining full responsibility for problem selection, product quality, and customer outcomes.
First 90 Days
During your first 90 days, you will be expected to:
Establish a clear product baseline and identify key opportunities and gaps.
Define and agree on launch scope, priorities, and acceptance criteria.
Demonstrate complete, high-quality priority workflows.
Establish onboarding, feedback, and product adoption processes.
Partner closely with Engineering to ensure migration and delivery readiness.
Develop a credible pilot and rollout plan based on measurable customer outcomes.

jobs.title: Director, Product Strategy & Transformation
jobs.text:
About the Role
Millions of professionals rely on Wolters Kluwer to make critical decisions across healthcare, tax, legal, financial services, compliance and corporate performance. As AI reshapes professional work, our customers expect software that is more intelligent, integrated and effective. Meeting those expectations requires rethinking how products are discovered, built, launched, measured and improved.
This newly created role reflects Wolters Kluwer's commitment to transforming how products are built in the age of AI. Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Product Strategy & Transformation, you will help lead that evolution from the Corporate Strategy Office. Working in a small enterprise team, you will partner with senior product, engineering, design and business leaders to strengthen the Product System and improve customer value, business outcomes and speed of innovation. A key focus will be advancing the Agentic Product Development Lifecycle (Agentic PDLC), using AI across product development. You will combine deep product expertise with a hands-on transformation mindset to implement and scale change.
How You Will Work
This is a senior individual-contributor role, leading through expertise, coaching, facilitation and influence. You will embed with business-unit teams on high-priority lighthouse initiatives, apply modern product practices and AI-enabled workflows, and turn proven approaches into reusable tools and operating practices for broader adoption.
The role can be based remotely in any country where Wolters Kluwer has an office and will require travel of approximately 35% to work directly with teams and stakeholders.
What You Will Do
Partner with senior product, engineering, design and business leaders to identify high-impact opportunities and connect product decisions to customer and business outcomes.
Define, pilot and scale Wolters Kluwer's Agentic PDLC and broader AI-enabled product development capabilities.
Lead lighthouse engagements across product strategy, discovery, experimentation, delivery, launch and measurement.
Embed with cross-functional teams to diagnose barriers, build trust and translate insight into practical change.
Coach product leaders and improve operating models, portfolio practices, governance and metrics.
Turn effective practices into repeatable tools, learning experiences and standards for enterprise adoption.
Establish success measures, demonstrate impact and use evidence to guide broader rollout.
Required Experience & Qualifications
8+ years of hands-on Product Management and/or Product Leadership experience in B2B software, SaaS or technology companies.
Ownership of strategy and outcomes for a substantial product, platform or portfolio, from customer discovery through delivery and measurement.
A track record of leading cross-functional product, engineering and design teams to meaningful customer and business outcomes.
Strong product craft across discovery, strategy, experimentation, prioritization, roadmaps, launch and measurement.
Recent hands-on experience building AI-enabled or agentic products, transforming product development workflows through AI, or both.
Ability to enter unfamiliar contexts, diagnose root causes, build trust and translate insight into action.
Proven influence on product direction, operating models or organizational effectiveness beyond a single team, without relying on formal authority.
Strong analytical, communication, storytelling and facilitation skills, with the judgment to simplify complexity and align senior leaders.
Preferred Experience
Leading product transformation, operating-model change or organizational scaling initiatives.
Coaching product leaders and strengthening product management practices.
Working across multiple businesses, portfolios or complex matrixed organizations.
Scaling reusable capabilities such as playbooks, metrics, communities of practice or leadership-development programs.
What Makes Someone Successful
Customer obsessed and focused on solving meaningful professional problems.
Passionate about product craft and motivated by helping multiple teams become more effective.
Curious, adaptable and energized by ambiguity, with high ownership and a bias toward action.
Strong product judgment balanced with evidence-based decision-making.
Pragmatic and hands-on, able to challenge the status quo, build followership and move from strategy to implementation.
Why This Role Matters
This role is designed for accomplished product leaders who have successfully built products, led teams and delivered meaningful business outcomes and are ready to extend their impact beyond a single product, platform or portfolio. Rather than owning one roadmap, you will help shape how product strategy, discovery, delivery and AI-enabled product development are practiced across a global software company. Your influence will be reflected not only in individual initiatives, but in stronger teams, faster learning, better decision-making and improved outcomes for the millions of professionals who rely on Wolters Kluwer every day.
If you are motivated by helping define product excellence, shaping AI-native ways of working and influencing the future of product development at enterprise scale, this is a unique opportunity to leave a lasting imprint across an entire global portfolio.
Our Interview Practices
To maintain a fair and genuine hiring process, we kindly ask that all candidates participate in interviews without the assistance of AI tools or external prompts. Our interview process is designed to assess your individual skills, experiences, and communication style. We value authenticity and want to ensure we’re getting to know you—not a digital assistant. To help maintain this integrity, we ask to remove virtual backgrounds and include in-person interviews in our hiring process. Please note that use of AI-generated responses or third-party support during interviews will be grounds for disqualification from the recruitment process.
Applicants may be required to appear onsite at a Wolters Kluwer office as part of the recruitment process.
Compensation:
$137,900.00 - $246,350.00 USDThis role is eligible for Bonus.
Compensation range listed is based on primary location of the position. Actual base salary offer is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skills, experience and actual hiring location. Your recruiter can share more information about the specific offer for the job location during the hiring process.
Additional Information:
Wolters Kluwer offers a wide variety of competitive benefits and programs to help meet your needs and balance your work and personal life, including but not limited to: Medical, Dental, & Vision Plans, 401(k), FSA/HSA, Commuter Benefits, Tuition Assistance Plan, Vacation and Sick Time, and Paid Parental Leave. Full details of our benefits are available upon request.

jobs.title: Vice President, Engineering
jobs.text:
AMP is applying AI-powered sortation at scale to modernize the world's recycling infrastructure and maximize the value in waste. AMP gives waste and recycling leaders the power to harness AI to reduce labor costs, increase resource recovery, and deliver more reliable operations. With hundreds of deployments across North America, Asia, and Europe, AMP’s technology offers a transformational solution to waste sortation and changes the fundamental economics of recycling.
Headquartered in Louisville, Colorado, the Denver Post and BuiltIn Colorado have recognized AMP as one of the state's top workplaces. AMP has operations and career opportunities outside of Atlanta, Cleveland, Portsmouth, Virginia, and Europe. We’re fostering an environment where passionate individuals can grow and create impact. We seek unconventional thinkers to join our mission to enable a world without waste; at AMP, your contributions have meaning and can spur change. With backing from top-tier investors and national recognition including North American Cleantech Company of the Year, we’re always seeking ways to better our operations, raising the bar on innovation, and looking to collaborate and improve in what we do. Learn more at AMPSortation.com.
AMP is looking for a VP of Engineering to lead the technology function of the company. This role will be managing a diverse team of software, robotics, mechanical, electrical, and infrastructure engineers and contractors. You will work closely with our CTO, CEO, and executive team to own, define, and execute on our product roadmap and strategy.
Responsibilities:
Technology Strategy & Leadership
Define and execute AMP's technology vision, strategy, and roadmap in support of the company's commercial and strategic objectives.
Align engineering teams around clear priorities, goals, and measures of success while maintaining accountability for results.
Balance short-term business needs with long-term technology investments to maximize company impact.
Organizational Leadership
Lead and scale AMP's engineering organization across Facility Engineering, R&D, and Software Infrastructure.
Build a high-performing culture known for quality, innovation, responsiveness, efficiency, and predictable execution.
Recruit, develop, mentor, and retain exceptional engineering talent and leaders.
Lead multidisciplinary teams spanning software, artificial intelligence, hardware, systems integration, manufacturing, and operations.
Product Development & Execution
Drive execution of hardware, software, and systems engineering programs, ensuring timely delivery of high-quality products and capabilities.
Establish engineering best practices, quality systems, and operating processes that support reliable deployments and scalable growth.
Ensure technology investments and roadmaps are aligned with customer needs, operational requirements, and business priorities.
Cross-Functional & Business Leadership
Partner with the executive team to shape and operationalize AMP's technology strategy.
Collaborate closely with Operations, Commercial, Product, and Customer teams to accelerate execution and deliver business value.
Own engineering budgets, resource planning, capital investments, and technology portfolio prioritization.
Establish and monitor key performance metrics across engineering, product delivery, quality, reliability, and operational efficiency.
Evaluate technology risks and opportunities, making decisions that balance innovation, execution, scalability, and financial performance.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related technical field; advanced degree preferred.
10+ years of engineering leadership experience in hardware-centric product organizations, including 4+ years at the Senior Director, VP, or equivalent executive level.
Experience leading multidisciplinary engineering organizations of 30+ engineers and technical leaders across hardware, software, systems, and operations.
Proven track record of delivering products and technology programs that create measurable business value.
Experience leading multiple product launches in fast-paced, agile environments.
Hands-on leadership across the full product lifecycle, including architecture, development, program management, quality, deployment, and operations.
Demonstrated success building high-performing teams, scalable engineering processes, and a culture of accountability and execution.
Strong leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills with high emotional intelligence and the ability to influence across all levels of an organization.
Ability to operate effectively in ambiguous environments, balancing innovation, technical debt, delivery commitments, and long-term investments. Strategic technology leader who connects engineering investments to business outcomes.
Strong operator with experience in budgeting, capital allocation, and portfolio prioritization.
Builder of high-performing organizations and leadership teams.
Customer- and business-oriented executive who balances innovation, operational excellence, and financial discipline.
Comfortable making high-impact decisions and influencing executives, customers, investors, and external partners.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience building, operating, or supporting manufacturing facilities enabled by internally developed technology.
Experience in one or more of the following areas:
Robotics
Machine Learning / AI
Embedded Systems
Industrial Automation, Manufacturing, and SCADA Systems
Cloud Infrastructure
DevOps and Platform Engineering
Product Management
Working Conditions/Physical Demands:
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times.
Travel Requirements:
25%
Equity Grant: The candidate selected for this role will be recommended for a stock option grant commensurate with the position and the candidate’s qualifications.
AMP provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. Applicants who identify with a historically underrepresented group are encouraged to apply. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.
Other duties:
Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Medical - The company covers between 78% to 100% of the premium for Cigna medical healthcare plans depending on the selection.
Dental, Vision, Short- and Long-Term Disability
Life Insurance: The company covers the cost of Basic Life / AD&D 1 x Salary, option to purchase additional through New York Life
Benefits start the day you start
HSA Eligible Health Plans, Company Monthly Contributions!
